fact_text: For PMTCT in pregnant women not requiring ART for their own health, Option B is preferred in Bangladesh: mother receives triple ARV prophylaxis starting as early as 14 weeks gestation continued until delivery or if breastfeeding, continued until 1 week after all infant exposure to breast milk ends; infant receives daily NVP or twice daily AZT from birth until 4 to 6 weeks of age. Option A is for HIV+ mothers with HBV co-infection not requiring treatment: antepartum twice daily AZT plus single dose NVP at labour onset plus twice daily AZT + 3TC during labour and delivery continued for 7 days postpartum; infant on breastfeeding receives daily NVP from birth until 1 week after breast milk exposure ends or 4 to 6 weeks if breastfeeding stops earlier; infants with no breastfeeding receive daily NVP from birth or single dose NVP at birth plus twice daily AZT from birth until 4 to 6 weeks.

fact_text: Abacavir (ABC) dose is 300 mg twice daily or 600 mg once daily with no food restrictions; adverse effects include hypersensitivity reaction in 3-5% (can be fatal) with symptoms of fever, rash, fatigue, nausea, vomiting, anorexia, respiratory symptoms (sore throat, cough, shortness of breath); re-challenging after reaction can be fatal; some studies show increased cardiovascular risk with ABC.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: ARV NRTI dose and adverse effects table
fact_text: Emtricitabine (FTC) dose is 200 mg once daily with no food restrictions; adverse effects are usually mild to moderate including diarrhea, headache, nausea, rash, and skin discoloration (hyperpigmentation of palms or soles); more severe side effects may include hepatotoxicity or lactic acidosis.
source_figure_or_table: ARV NRTI dose and adverse effects table

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: ARV NRTI dose and adverse effects table
fact_text: Lamivudine (3TC) dose is 150 mg twice daily or 300 mg once daily with no food restrictions; adverse effects are minimal toxicity.
source_figure_or_table: ARV NRTI dose and adverse effects table

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: NNRTI dose and adverse effects table (partial)
fact_text: Nevirapine (NVP) dose is 200 mg once daily for 14 days followed by 200 mg twice daily with no food restrictions; adverse effects include hepatitis (usually within 12 weeks), life-threatening hepatic toxicity, skin rash that can progress to Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis (TEN); patients developing hepatic toxicity require close monitoring.
source_figure_or_table: NNRTI dose and adverse effects table (partial)

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: ARV NRTI dose and adverse effects table
fact_text: Tenofovir (TDF) dose is 300 mg once daily with no food restrictions; adverse effects include asthenia, headache, diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, flatulence, renal insufficiency, Fanconi syndrome, osteomalacia, and potential decreased bone mineral density; dosage adjustment is recommended in renal insufficiency; severe acute hepatitis exacerbation may occur in HBV-coinfected patients who discontinue TDF.
source_figure_or_table: ARV NRTI dose and adverse effects table

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: ARV NRTI dose and adverse effects table
fact_text: Zidovudine (ZDV, AZT) dose is 300 mg twice daily with no food restrictions; adverse effects include anaemia, neutropenia, bone marrow suppression, gastrointestinal intolerance, headache, insomnia, myopathy, lactic acidosis, and skin & nail hyperpigmentation.
source_figure_or_table: ARV NRTI dose and adverse effects table

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: Protease inhibitors dose and adverse effects table
fact_text: Atazanavir/ritonavir (ATV/r) dose is 300 mg atazanavir plus 100 mg ritonavir once daily; recommended to take with food; adverse effects include hyperbilirubinemia, less lipid problems than LPV/r, fat maldistribution, hyperglycemia, nephrolithiasis; interacts with acid blocking agents requiring dose adjustment; do not co-administer with proton pump inhibitors such as omeprazole.
source_figure_or_table: Protease inhibitors dose and adverse effects table

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: Efavirenz dose and adverse effects table
fact_text: Efavirenz (EFV) dose is 600 mg once daily, preferably at bedtime to reduce CNS side effects; avoid taking after high fat meals; CNS adverse effects include dizziness, somnolence, insomnia, confusion, hallucinations, agitation, personality change; rash less common than with nevirapine; EFV is not recommended in the first trimester of pregnancy.
source_figure_or_table: Efavirenz dose and adverse effects table

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: Protease inhibitors dose and adverse effects table
fact_text: Lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) heat stable tablets dose is 200 mg lopinavir/50 mg ritonavir fixed dose tablet, 2 tablets twice daily; no food restrictions; adverse effects include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, abnormal lipid profiles, glucose intolerance; contraindicated with Simvastatin due to risk of rhabdomyolysis and severe kidney failure.
source_figure_or_table: Protease inhibitors dose and adverse effects table

source_section: Protease inhibitors dose and adverse effects table
fact_text: Saquinavir/ritonavir (SQV/r) dose is 1000 mg saquinavir plus 100 mg ritonavir twice daily; no food restrictions; adverse effects include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, headache, photosensitivity.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: EFV is not recommended during the first trimester of pregnancy or in women with high pregnancy potential unless effective contraception is used; discontinuation is advised if pregnancy occurs on EFV.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Fanconi syndrome is a proximal renal tubule disease causing loss of glucose, amino acids, uric acid, phosphate, and bicarbonate in urine instead of reabsorption, leading to proximal renal tubular acidosis and bone disease resembling rickets despite adequate vitamin D and calcium.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Lactic acidosis is a metabolic acidosis caused by low pH in tissues and blood with lactate buildup, often due to hypoxia or impaired cellular respiration, leading to symptoms like rapid breathing, drowsiness, irregular heartbeat, and weakness, especially in limbs.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Osteomalacia is bone softening due to defective mineralization from inadequate phosphorus and calcium, often caused by vitamin D deficiency, presenting with diffuse bone pain, muscle weakness, and fragility.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Renal insufficiency is defined as decreased glomerular filtration rate and is typically detected by elevated serum creatinine levels.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Rhabdomyolysis is rapid skeletal muscle breakdown releasing harmful products like myoglobin into the bloodstream, which can cause kidney damage and failure.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: stevens-johnson syndrome (sjs) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (ten)
condition_aliases: stevens-johnson syndrome (sjs) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (ten)
fact_text: SJS and TEN are life-threatening hypersensitivity reactions causing epidermal cell death and skin separation from dermis, mainly drug-induced, requiring urgent recognition and management.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Availability of voluntary and confidential counseling and reliable, inexpensive HIV diagnostic tests is essential for ART services.
Provision of ART adherence counseling is required.
Adequate health infrastructure must support management of opportunistic infections and ensure availability of affordable treatment and prophylaxis drugs.

Laboratory facilities should monitor CD4 count, viral load (if available), liver function tests, urea, creatinine, electrolytes, complete blood count, pregnancy test, acid fast bacilli, and chest X-ray.

Clinicians and nurses require training to perform basic clinical assessment including past medical history, current and past HIV-related illnesses, coexisting medical conditions, and current signs and symptoms.
Support social networks such as PLHIV support groups, PLHIV networks, and NGOs to help patient adherence.
If social networks are absent, psycho-social services including counseling and adherence support should be provided via government, NGOs, or private/philanthropic sectors.
Strengthen health and psycho-social services across continuum of care from home to community health centers to district/city hospitals with flexible and timely referral coordination.
Provide material and psycho-social support for patients on ART at various care levels.
Ensure reliable, long-term, and regular supply of ARV drugs, reagents, and test kits.
fact_text: ART services require voluntary confidential counseling, reliable HIV testing, adherence counseling, adequate infrastructure for OI management, lab monitoring (CD4, viral load, LFTs, CBC, pregnancy test, AFB, chest X-ray), trained clinicians for clinical assessment, social network support for adherence, psycho-social services if networks absent, continuum of care coordination, material and psycho-social support, and reliable ARV drug supply.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: WHO Clinical Stage 1 in adults and adolescents is defined as asymptomatic or persistent generalized lymphadenopathy.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: WHO Clinical Stage 2 in adults and adolescents includes moderate unexplained weight loss (under 10% of presumed or measured body weight), recurrent respiratory tract infections (sinusitis, tonsillitis, otitis media, pharyngitis), herpes zoster, and angular cheilitis.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Baseline laboratory tests before ART initiation should include CD4 cell count to assess immune status.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Complete blood count including hemoglobin percentage is recommended as a baseline test before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C screening tests should be performed for current or past people who inject drugs (PWID) before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Liver function tests including ALT/SGPT should be done if clinically indicated before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Serum creatinine and other kidney function tests (urea, electrolytes) should be performed if clinically indicated before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Urine pregnancy test should be done if indicated in females before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Blood sugar level should be measured if clinically indicated before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Chest X-ray and sputum examination for acid-fast bacilli (AFB) should be done if tuberculosis is suspected before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: For women, cervical pap smear or other cervical cancer screening methods should be done if available before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Urine routine and microscopic examination including urinalysis to assess proteinuria should be done if indicated before ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Major goals of ART include maximal and durable viral load suppression, restoration or preservation of immunologic function, reduction of HIV-related morbidity and mortality, improvement of quality of life, prevention of mother-to-child transmission (PMTCT), and provision of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: WHO clinical staging for HIV infection defines stage 3 by presence of conditions such as recurrent oral ulceration, papular pruritic eruptions, seborrhoeic dermatitis, fungal nail infections, unexplained severe weight loss >10%, chronic diarrhea >1 month, persistent fever >1 month, persistent oral candidiasis, oral hairy leukoplakia, pulmonary tuberculosis, severe bacterial infections, acute necrotizing ulcerative stomatitis/gingivitis/periodontitis, and unexplained severe cytopenias. Stage 4 includes HIV wasting syndrome, Pneumocystis jiroveci pneumonia, recurrent severe bacterial pneumonia, chronic herpes simplex infection >1 month or visceral, oesophageal candidiasis, extrapulmonary tuberculosis, Kaposi sarcoma, cytomegalovirus infection (retinitis or other organs except liver/spleen/lymph nodes), CNS toxoplasmosis, HIV encephalopathy, extrapulmonary cryptococcosis including meningitis, disseminated non-tuberculous mycobacterial infection, progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, chronic cryptosporidiosis, chronic isosporiasis, disseminated mycosis, recurrent septicemia, lymphoma, invasive cervical carcinoma, atypical disseminated leishmaniasis, and symptomatic HIV-associated nephropathy or cardiomyopathy.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Start ART irrespective of CD4 cell count in patients with active tuberculosis disease.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Start ART irrespective of CD4 cell count in patients with hepatitis B virus infection requiring treatment.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Start ART in asymptomatic individuals including pregnant women if WHO clinical stage 1 and CD4 count is ≤350 cells/mm3.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Start ART in symptomatic individuals including pregnant women if WHO clinical stage 2 and CD4 count is ≤350 cells/mm3.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Start ART irrespective of CD4 cell count in individuals with WHO clinical stage 3 or 4 disease.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Ritonavir combined with another protease inhibitor boosts plasma concentration, allowing reduced dose frequency and pill burden; PI-based regimens are recommended as second-line options in Bangladesh.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Preferred ART regimens combine an NNRTI or protease inhibitor with 2 NRTIs for potent viral suppression.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Single or dual drug ART regimens are not recommended except for post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Preferred first-line ART regimens for adults and adolescents include AZT + 3TC + EFV or NVP, or TDF + 3TC + EFV or NVP; fixed-dose combinations are recommended.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Possible NRTI combinations include: Zidovudine + Lamivudine, Abacavir + Lamivudine, Tenofovir + Lamivudine, and Tenofovir + Emtricitabine.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Preferred first-line ART regimens for pregnant women are AZT + 3TC + NVP or AZT + 3TC + EFV; EFV should not be initiated during the first trimester.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: pregnant women with prior pmtct exposure
condition_aliases: pregnant women with prior pmtct exposure
fact_text: In pregnant women with prior exposure to PMTCT regimens, ART regimen choice should be guided by additional considerations (details not provided on this page).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Recommended ART combinations include: 1) 2 NRTIs + NNRTI, 2) 2 NRTIs + PI, or 3) 3 NRTIs; only two such combinations are recommended: ZDV+3TC+ABC and ZDV+3TC+TDF.

condition: adverse drug reaction: drug eruptions including stevens-johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis
condition_aliases: severe cutaneous adverse reactions to nvp or efv
adverse drug reaction: drug eruptions including stevens-johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis
trigger_evidence: Drug eruption mild to severe including Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis
alternative_medicines: Switch from NVP to EFV in mild cases
recommended_advice: In mild cases, EFV rash often resolves spontaneously in 3-5 days without ART change; if moderate rash without mucosal/systemic signs, consider single NNRTI substitution from NVP to EFV
referral_criteria: Severe drug eruption requiring ART discontinuation and supportive care
admission_criteria: Severe Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis
fact_text: For drug eruptions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome or toxic epidermal necrolysis caused by NVP (more common) or EFV (less common): mild EFV rash often resolves in 3-5 days without ART change; moderate rash without mucosal/systemic signs may be managed by switching from NVP to EFV; moderate/severe cases require ART discontinuation and supportive care; after resolution, resume ART with bPI-based regimen or triple NRTI if no other option.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition_aliases: hiv with hepatitis b virus coinfection
recommended_advice: Use two ARVs with anti-HBV activity in regimen
contraindications_or_cautions: Consider HBsAg screening before ART, especially if TDF is not preferred first-line NRTI
fact_text: For HIV/HBV coinfection, preferred ART regimen is TDF + 3TC + EFV; alternative is TDF + 3TC + NVP; HBsAg screening should be considered before ART, especially if TDF is not used; regimen must include two ARVs active against HBV.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Initiate ART as soon as possible within first 8 weeks after starting TB treatment
fact_text: For HIV/TB coinfection, preferred ART regimen is AZT + 3TC + EFV; NVP is an acceptable alternative to EFV; triple NRTI regimen can be used only if both EFV and NVP are contraindicated; ART should be initiated as soon as possible within first 8 weeks after starting TB treatment.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: ART clinical and laboratory monitoring schedule after initiation: first month every two weeks; second and third months every one month; from fourth month onwards every three months.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Abacavir (ABC) hypersensitivity reaction: substitute with AZT or TDF.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Efavirenz (EFV) severe central nervous system toxicity or potential neural tube abnormalities if used in first trimester of pregnancy: substitute with NVP or ABC or any protease inhibitor (PI).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Nevirapine (NVP) hepatitis or hypersensitivity reaction including severe or life-threatening rash (e.g., Stevens-Johnson syndrome): substitute with EFV or ABC or any protease inhibitor (PI).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Tenofovir (TDF) renal toxicity (renal tubular dysfunction): substitute with AZT or ABC. For lactic acidosis, substitute with TDF or ABC.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Zidovudine (AZT) severe anaemia or neutropenia and severe gastrointestinal intolerance: substitute with TDF or ABC. For lactic acidosis, substitute with TDF or ABC.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: alt > 5 times upper limit of normal
condition_aliases: alt > 5 times upper limit of normal
fact_text: If ALT is more than five times the basal level, discontinue ART and monitor liver function. After resolution, restart ART replacing the causative drug, for example, replace Nevirapine (NVP) with Efavirenz (EFV).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: In case of lactic acidosis with any NRTI, discontinue ART and provide supportive treatment. After resolution, ART can be resumed with Tenofovir (TDF).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: For early lipoatrophy or lipodystrophy suspected to be caused by NRTIs, replace the suspected ARV drug such as Tenofovir (TDF) or Zidovudine (AZT) early.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Neuropsychiatric changes caused by Efavirenz (EFV) are usually self-limited and do not require ART discontinuation. If intolerable, replace EFV with Nevirapine (NVP) or a boosted protease inhibitor (PI) without stopping ART.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: renal toxicity (renal tubular dysfunction) due to tenofovir (tdf)
condition_aliases: renal toxicity (renal tubular dysfunction) due to tenofovir (tdf)
fact_text: In case of renal toxicity or renal tubular dysfunction caused by Tenofovir (TDF), consider substitution with Zidovudine (AZT).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: severe anaemia (hb <7.0 g/dl) and/or neutropenia (anc <750 cells/mm3)
condition_aliases: severe anaemia (hb <7.0 g/dl) and/or neutropenia (anc <750 cells/mm3)
fact_text: In patients with severe anaemia (Hb <7.0 g/dl) and/or neutropenia (ANC <750 cells/mm3), replace the current ARV with one having minimal or no bone marrow toxicity such as Tenofovir (TDF), and consider blood transfusion.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Adherence to ARV drugs is necessary for optimal virological suppression
Over 95% of doses should be taken for optimal viral suppression
fact_text: A high degree of adherence to ARV drugs is necessary for optimal virological suppression; studies indicate over 95% of doses should be taken.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: For patients not responding to treatment, viral load and resistance testing are recommended whenever feasible to confirm treatment failure.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: Laboratory monitoring after initiation of ART
followup_monitoring: Use viral load as targeted approach to confirm suspected treatment failure based on immunological or clinical criteria
If resources permit, use viral load as routine approach every 6 months to detect failure earlier
contraindications_or_cautions: Hb monitoring recommended in patients at high risk of AZT toxicity (low CD4 or low BMI)
Creatinine clearance recommended in patients at high risk of TDF toxicity (renal disease, older age, low BMI, diabetes, hypertension, or boosted PI use)
ALT monitoring recommended in patients at high risk of NVP toxicity (women with CD4 >250)
fact_text: At ART initiation, CD4 count is recommended for all patients; Hb for those on AZT, creatinine clearance for those on TDF, and ALT for those on NVP should be measured if resources permit. CD4 count should be repeated every 6 months. Viral load testing every 6 months is recommended if available, especially for women exposed to sd-NVP with tail4 within 12 months and without tail within 6 months. Viral load is used to confirm treatment failure earlier than immunological or clinical criteria.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
trigger_evidence: HIV patients with drug use background
recommended_tests: Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C testing
fact_text: In PLHIV with drug use background, Hepatitis B and Hepatitis C testing should be performed to identify co-infection and determine need for TDF-containing ART.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Adherence must be assured before ART initiation; patients should fully understand its importance.
Adherence counselling and patient education should be conducted at every follow-up visit.
fact_text: Adherence counselling is essential before ART initiation and at every follow-up visit to ensure patient understanding and reduce risk of virological failure.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Preparatory adherence counselling visits should be conducted before ART start, including use of mock pills if possible.
The treating physician and counsellor should jointly assess patient readiness to start ART after the final preparatory visit.
fact_text: Preparatory adherence counselling visits with mock pills should be done before ART start, with joint physician and counsellor assessment of patient readiness after the final visit.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Pre-ART adherence counselling should include clinical assessment, HIV knowledge exploration, ART and OI treatment introduction, consequences of non-adherence, barriers to adherence, transmission risk education, and discussion of a treatment buddy.
fact_text: Visit 1 pre-ART adherence counselling should cover clinical assessment, HIV and ART knowledge, consequences of non-adherence, barriers, transmission risk, and treatment buddy concept.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Visit 2 pre-ART adherence counselling should include clinician feedback on prior assessments, review of client understanding and barriers, treatment plan review including correct dosing and timing, and a test run of the regimen with empty capsules to record missed doses and reasons.
fact_text: Visit 2 pre-ART adherence counselling includes clinician feedback, client understanding review, barrier reassessment, treatment plan review with correct dose/time, and a test run of regimen with empty capsules to record missed doses and reasons.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Visit 3 pre-ART adherence counselling should review client understanding from prior sessions, reinforce complexity of treatment, and review problem-solving strategies and adherence tools such as reminder cards and recording tools.
fact_text: Visit 3 pre-ART adherence counselling reviews client understanding, reinforces treatment complexity, and familiarizes client with problem-solving strategies and adherence reminder/recording tools.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
frequency: within 1-2 weeks after ART start and at regular intervals throughout ART
recommended_advice: Follow-up adherence counselling visits should occur within 1-2 weeks after ART initiation and continue regularly throughout treatment to address changing barriers and support needs.

Counselling sessions should review treatment experience, assess need for clinician referral (usually for side effects), monitor adherence over a defined period, identify and solve adherence barriers, review adherence related to transmission risk reduction, and conduct psychosocial assessment.
followup_monitoring: Adherence counselling should be ongoing and interactive to provide effective support as patients adjust to treatment and face new challenges.
fact_text: Adherence counselling should start within 1-2 weeks after ART initiation and continue regularly, including reviewing treatment experience, side effects, adherence monitoring, barrier solutions, transmission risk adherence, and psychosocial assessment.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: After the first month of ART, adherence measurement and counselling should be done monthly or whenever the patient comes to collect ARV.
followup_monitoring: Review information from previous visits and assess patient understanding at each visit.
fact_text: After the first month on ART, adherence measurement and counselling should be performed monthly or at every ARV collection visit.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_advice: Pill count is recommended to calculate adherence at each follow-up visit by asking the patient to bring remaining pills from previous visits and using the formula: Adherence (%) = [(Total pills to be taken - Pills missed) / Total pills to be taken] x 100.
followup_monitoring: Adherence should be above 95%.
fact_text: Pill count adherence calculation is recommended at each follow-up visit using the formula: Adherence (%) = [(Total pills to be taken - Pills missed) / Total pills to be taken] x 100; adherence should be above 95%.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
frequency: 48-72 hours after ART start, then at 2 weeks, then monthly
recommended_advice: First follow-up visit after ART initiation should be within 48-72 hours, then at 2 weeks, and then monthly for adherence measurement and counselling.
followup_monitoring: During each follow-up visit, review information from previous visits and assess patient understanding.
fact_text: After starting ART, the first follow-up visit should be within 48-72 hours, then at 2 weeks, and monthly thereafter for adherence measurement and counselling.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: ART failure criteria after ≥6 months on ART include: clinical failure defined as new/recurrent WHO stage 4 condition excluding IRIS and some stage 3 conditions; immunological failure defined as CD4 fall to baseline or below, 50% fall from peak, or persistent CD4 <100 cells/mm3 without infection; virological failure defined as plasma viral load >5000 copies/ml.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Treatment success criteria include: clinical improvement to WHO stage 1 or 2 by 12 weeks; CD4 increase by 50-100 cells/mm3 within 6-12 months (optimal >100 cells/mm3 increase); viral load <5000 copies/ml at 24-48 weeks post ART initiation.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_medicines: Ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitors (RTV-PIs) are preferred for second-line treatment.
avoid_medicines: Do not switch from one NNRTI to another (e.g., do not replace EFV with NVP or vice versa) at time of failure due to high cross-resistance risk.
fact_text: Ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitors (RTV-PIs) are preferred for second-line ART; do not switch between NNRTIs at failure due to high cross-resistance risk.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: In ART treatment failure, switch the entire regimen from first-line to second-line; do not change or add a single drug to a failing regimen.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Second-line ART regimens should contain a minimum of three active drugs, including at least one from a new drug class to minimize cross-resistance.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011

condition_aliases: pregnancy in women living with hiv
recommended_advice: WHO recommends vaginal delivery for women living with HIV in all conditions except obstetric emergencies.
Start prophylaxis for mother and baby immediately on first contact.

To reduce mother-to-child transmission (MTCT) during vaginal delivery, minimize duration of labor and obstetric interventions such as vaginal examinations, episiotomies, tears, and instrumental delivery.
Avoid operative or manipulative vaginal deliveries (forceps, vacuum extraction, breech extraction, multiple pregnancy manipulations) due to increased risk of mixing fetal and maternal blood.

Elective cesarean section is suggested internationally for HIV-infected women who have not achieved adequate viral suppression by 38 weeks gestation, but in Bangladesh this decision depends on availability, accessibility, and quality of institutional care.

Due to limited viral load testing in Bangladesh, mode of delivery decisions should be made jointly by obstetrician and ART clinician considering ARV prophylaxis/treatment duration, clinical and immunological status, and obstetric conditions.
fact_text: WHO recommends vaginal delivery for women living with HIV except in obstetric emergencies; prophylaxis for mother and baby should start immediately; minimize labor duration and obstetric interventions to reduce MTCT; avoid operative vaginal deliveries due to blood mixing risk; elective cesarean section may be considered if viral suppression is inadequate by 38 weeks but decision depends on local resources and clinical context.

source_section: Dosage of first line ARVs for infants and children table
fact_text: AZT syrup dose for 6-10 kg infants is 9 ml twice daily; 3TC syrup dose is 4 ml twice daily; NVP syrup dose is 8 ml twice daily.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: infants and children less than 3 years of age with tuberculosis
condition_aliases: infants and children less than 3 years of age with tuberculosis
source_section: Infants and children with specific conditions table
fact_text: Preferred ART regimen for infants and children <3 years with tuberculosis is NVP + AZT + 3TC; alternative regimen is AZT + 3TC + ABC.
source_figure_or_table: Infants and children with specific conditions table

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: infants exposed to maternal or infant nvp or other nnrtis used for maternal treatment or pmtct
condition_aliases: infants exposed to maternal or infant nvp or other nnrtis used for maternal treatment or pmtct
source_section: Groups of infants ART regimen table
fact_text: For infants exposed to maternal or infant NVP or other NNRTIs used for maternal treatment or PMTCT, preferred ART regimen is LPV/r + AZT + 3TC; alternative regimen is NVP + AZT + 3TC only if PIs are not available and not feasible.
source_figure_or_table: Groups of infants ART regimen table

condition: infants not exposed to arvs or unknown exposure to maternal/infant arvs

source_section: Groups of infants ART regimen table
fact_text: For infants not exposed to ARVs or with unknown exposure to maternal or infant ARVs, preferred ART regimen is LPV/r + AZT + 3TC; alternative regimen is NVP + AZT + 3TC only if PIs are not available and not feasible.
source_figure_or_table: Groups of infants ART regimen table

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: children not yet eligible for art
condition_aliases: children not yet eligible for art
fact_text: CD4 monitoring for children not yet eligible for ART should be performed every six months to assess eligibility for treatment or co-trimoxazole prophylaxis; percent CD4 is preferred for children under 5 years rather than absolute CD4 count.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: children not yet eligible for art
condition_aliases: children not yet eligible for art
fact_text: Children not yet eligible for ART require more frequent clinical and laboratory monitoring than adults due to rapid disease progression; clinical evaluation every 3 to 6 months minimum including baseline parameters is recommended.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: For children on ART, clinical follow-up visits should occur at weeks 2, 4, 8, and then every 4 weeks for infants during the first year; for older children, visits at weeks 2, 4, 8, 12 and then every 2-3 months after stabilization on therapy.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Growth, development, and nutrition of children on ART should be monitored monthly using standard pediatric practice.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: CD4 monitoring is recommended at 6 months after ART initiation and every 6 months thereafter for children on ART.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Viral load testing is not essential but should be used whenever possible to confirm suspected treatment failure in children on ART.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Baseline hemoglobin and white cell count (if available) should be measured before ART initiation; hemoglobin should be rechecked at week 8 after starting AZT-containing regimens or more frequently if symptoms indicate toxicity.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Lopinavir/ritonavir (LPV/r) syrup dosing for children is weight-based: 1 ml for 6 kg, 1.5 ml for 10 kg, 2 ml for 14 kg, 2.5 ml for 15-20 kg, and 3 ml for 20-25 kg. WHO recommends 1.5 ml twice daily for infants/children 4-6 kg.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Nevirapine (NVP) tablet dose for children varies by body weight: 200 mg for all weight bands shown (3-6 kg to 20-25 kg) with specific tablet fractions for heavier weights (e.g., 1 tab for 10-14 kg, 1/2 tab for 15-20 kg).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Laboratory monitoring for ART toxicity in children should be symptom-directed if testing is available.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Switch to second-line ART is recommended in children with clinical failure (WHO stage 3 or 4 events after ≥24 weeks on ART), immunological failure (CD4 <200 cells/mm3 or CD4% <10% for ages 2 to <5 years; CD4 <100 cells/mm3 for ≥5 years after ≥24 weeks on ART), or virological failure (viral load >5000 copies/ml after ≥24 weeks on ART) in treatment-adherent children.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: second-line art regimen choice after first-line failure
condition_aliases: second-line art regimen choice after first-line failure
recommended_medicines: LPV/r (lopinavir/ritonavir) as preferred boosted protease inhibitor for second-line ART
AZT+3TC (zidovudine + lamivudine) as preferred NRTI backbone after failure on ABC+3TC
ABC+3TC as preferred NRTI backbone after failure on AZT+3TC
NNRTI plus 2 NRTIs as preferred second-line if child was started on PI regimen
fact_text: After failure on a first-line NNRTI-based regimen, second-line ART should be a boosted protease inhibitor (LPV/r preferred) plus 2 NRTIs. After failure on a first-line regimen of AZT+3TC, ABC+3TC is preferred for second-line NRTI backbone, and vice versa. If the child started on a PI regimen, the preferred second-line is NNRTI plus 2 NRTIs.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for HIV-exposed infants in Bangladesh up to six months of age, with introduction of complementary feeding thereafter under full ARV coverage or prophylaxis after six months to minimize MTCT risk. Breastfeeding should continue up to one year with ARV coverage, and gradual cessation is advised starting at 11 months, completing by one year. Mothers on prophylaxis should continue ARV for one week after stopping breastfeeding.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: For children 24 months or older, preferred first line regimens are NVP+AZT+3TC (preferred), EFV+AZT+3TC (preferred if >3 years), or NVP+ABC+3TC. Preferred second line regimens are LPV/r + ABC+3TC or LPV/r + AZT+3TC.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: children and adolescents with hepatitis b
condition_aliases: children and adolescents with hepatitis b
fact_text: For children and adolescents with Hepatitis B, preferred first line regimen is TDF + 3TC + EFV. Preferred second line regimen is LPV/r + AZT + 3TC.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: children and adolescents with severe anemia
condition_aliases: children and adolescents with severe anemia
fact_text: For children and adolescents with severe anemia, first line regimen is NVP+ABC+3TC. Preferred second line regimen is LPV/r + 3TC + NRTI (decision should be made consulting a pediatrician and considering availability).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: For children and adolescents with TB, preferred first line regimens are EFV+AZT+3TC (preferred if >3 years), NVP+AZT+3TC (if <3 years), or AZT+3TC+ABC. Preferred second line regimens are LPV/r + ABC+3TC or LPV/r + AZT+3TC.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: infants and children less than 24 months exposed to nnrti
condition_aliases: infants and children less than 24 months exposed to nnrti
fact_text: For infants and children less than 24 months exposed to NNRTI, preferred first line regimen is LPV/r + 2NRTIs (LPV/r + AZT+3TC preferred). Preferred second line regimen is NNRTI + 2NRTIs (NVP + AZT + 3TC).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: infants and children less than 24 months not exposed to arv
condition_aliases: infants and children less than 24 months not exposed to arv
fact_text: For infants and children less than 24 months not exposed to ARV, preferred second line regimen after first line NVP+2NRTIs (NVP+AZT+3TC or NVP+ABC+3TC) is LPV/r + 2NRTIs (LPV/r + ABC+3TC or LPV/r + AZT+3TC).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: infants and children less than 24 months with unknown arv exposure
condition_aliases: infants and children less than 24 months with unknown arv exposure
fact_text: For infants and children less than 24 months with unknown ARV exposure, first line regimen is NVP + 2NRTIs (NVP+AZT+3TC or NVP+ABC+3TC). Preferred second line regimen is LPV/r + 2NRTIs (LPV/r + ABC+3TC or LPV/r + AZT+3TC).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Mothers of HIV-infected infants and young children are strongly encouraged to exclusively breastfeed for 6 months and continue breastfeeding as per general population recommendations (up to 2 years or beyond).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: HIV-infected children should have routine nutritional status assessment including weight and height at scheduled visits, especially after ART initiation, during growth monitoring and immunization visits.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: HIV-infected children should receive one recommended daily allowance (RDA) of micronutrients daily; if diet is insufficient or deficiency suspected, supplementation should be provided as per uninfected child guidelines.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Severely malnourished HIV-infected children should be managed according to guidelines for uninfected severely malnourished children, with energy and protein requirements based on individual symptoms and needs.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: hiv-infected children symptomatic or with weight loss
condition_aliases: hiv-infected children symptomatic or with weight loss
fact_text: HIV-infected children on or off ART who are symptomatic or have weight loss or poor growth should receive additional energy intake: asymptomatic children require 10% more energy than healthy peers; symptomatic without weight loss require 20-30% more energy; symptomatic with weight loss require 50-100% more energy than healthy children.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: HIV-infected children with diarrhoea should receive zinc supplementation as part of management, following guidelines for uninfected children.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: hiv-infected infants and children aged 6-59 months
condition_aliases: hiv-infected infants and children aged 6-59 months
fact_text: HIV-infected infants and children aged 6 to 59 months should receive high-dose vitamin A supplementation every 6 months as per uninfected child guidelines.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Adherence preparation should start as early as possible before ART initiation but should not delay treatment if the child is at risk of disease progression or death; adherence must be assessed at every visit with parental, caregiver, and child-related issues addressed, early intervention for adherence problems, and use of child-friendly formulations and practical tools like pill boxes, calendars, or diaries to support adherence.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: children with symptomatic or severe immunodeficiency (cd4% less than 15%)
condition_aliases: children with symptomatic or severe immunodeficiency (cd4% less than 15%)
fact_text: Children with symptomatic or severe immunodeficiency defined as CD4 percentage less than 15% should receive antiretroviral therapy before receiving vaccinations with attenuated live vaccines such as measles, mumps, and rubella.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: infants and children living with or exposed to hiv with unclear hiv status
condition_aliases: infants and children living with or exposed to hiv with unclear hiv status
fact_text: Infants and children living with or exposed to HIV with unclear HIV status should receive an extra dose of measles vaccine at 6 months of age.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: hiv infection in infants and children
condition_aliases: hiv infection in infants and children
fact_text: Infants and children living with HIV should not receive Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccination for tuberculosis due to contraindication.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Oral polio vaccine (OPV) is not contraindicated in HIV positive children, but is not recommended in settings where polio has been eradicated or transmission risk is very low; in high transmission risk settings or where importation risk is high, OPV is recommended despite concerns about prolonged virus excretion.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Screen all people living with HIV for active tuberculosis as per National TB HIV Guidelines.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Start ART in all HIV-infected individuals with active tuberculosis regardless of CD4 cell count.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Efavirenz (EFV) is the preferred NNRTI for patients starting ART during TB treatment due to less interaction with rifampicin; standard EFV dose is 600 mg daily without dose increase.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Drug interactions between rifampicin and boosted protease inhibitors prohibit concomitant use of standard therapies for both HIV and TB.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: Preferred and alternative ART regimens for HIV/TB coinfection
fact_text: Alternative ART regimens for HIV/TB coinfected patients include AZT + 3TC + NVP, AZT + 3TC + ABC, or AZT + 3TC + TDF.
source_figure_or_table: Preferred and alternative ART regimens for HIV/TB coinfection

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: Preferred and alternative ART regimens for HIV/TB coinfection
fact_text: Preferred ART regimen for HIV/TB coinfected patients in Bangladesh is AZT + 3TC + EFV.
source_figure_or_table: Preferred and alternative ART regimens for HIV/TB coinfection

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: Start TB treatment first, then initiate ART as soon as possible after TB therapy is tolerated, ideally between 2 to 8 weeks after starting TB treatment.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: hiv with active tuberculosis on rifampicin
condition_aliases: hiv with active tuberculosis on rifampicin
fact_text: In presence of rifampicin, no lead-in dose of nevirapine (NVP) is required when used in ART regimens for HIV/TB coinfected patients.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: hiv with active tuberculosis unable to tolerate efavirenz
condition_aliases: hiv with active tuberculosis unable to tolerate efavirenz
fact_text: For HIV/TB coinfected patients unable to tolerate efavirenz, alternative ART regimens include: (1) an NVP-based regimen, or (2) a triple NNRTI regimen (AZT + 3TC + ABC or AZT + 3TC + TDF).

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_medicines: Start TDF and 3TC (or FTC)-containing ART regimens in all HIV/HBV co-infected patients needing treatment
Use at least two agents active against HBV, specifically TDF plus 3TC or FTC
fact_text: Start ART in all HIV/HBV co-infected patients requiring treatment for chronic active hepatitis B regardless of CD4 count or WHO stage; use TDF plus 3TC or FTC-containing regimens with at least two agents active against HBV.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
recommended_medicines: ART initiation in HIV/HCV co-infected patients should follow same recommendations as for HIV mono-infection
fact_text: Initiate ART in HIV/HCV co-infected patients using the same principles and recommendations as for HIV mono-infected individuals.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
condition: people who inject drugs (pwid) on methadone substitution
condition_aliases: people who inject drugs (pwid) on methadone substitution
recommended_medicines: Integrate directly administered/observed ART and TB therapy with opioid agonist maintenance treatment for PWID on methadone to improve adherence
recommended_advice: Provide opioid agonist maintenance treatment and ART/TB therapy at the same location to enhance adherence and reduce unsafe opioid injection
contraindications_or_cautions: Some ARVs interact with methadone; dose adjustments or monitoring may be required
fact_text: For PWID on methadone substitution, integrate directly observed ART and TB therapy with opioid agonist maintenance treatment at the same location to improve adherence; be aware of ARV-methadone interactions and adjust therapy accordingly.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
fact_text: ZDV requires monitoring for adverse effects including anemia, myalgia, bone marrow suppression, fatigue, headache, and vomiting; methadone significantly increases ZDV blood levels. EFV and NVP can cause opioid withdrawal by decreasing methadone concentration, often requiring methadone dose increase; withdrawal may be delayed 2-3 weeks after starting EFV or NVP. ATV/r, LPV/r, SQV/r may cause opioid withdrawal but usually no methadone dose adjustment is needed; monitor clinically.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
dose_or_duration: PEP should be started as soon as possible, preferably within 2 hours of exposure; not recommended after 72 hours
recommended_advice: Provide first aid by washing exposed area thoroughly with running water and mild soap
Do not squeeze wound to express blood
Do not apply antiseptics to injury area as it may increase HIV transmission risk by enhancing local inflammation
fact_text: Post Exposure Prophylaxis (PEP) for HIV should be started as soon as possible, preferably within 2 hours of occupational exposure, and is not recommended after 72 hours. First aid includes thorough washing with running water and mild soap; squeezing the wound or applying antiseptics is not recommended as it may increase HIV transmission risk.

source_title: National Guidelines of Antiretroviral Therapy, Bangladesh, 2011
source_section: Recommended HIV regimen according to the risk of HIV transmission
recommended_tests: HIV antibody testing at 6 weeks, 3 months, and 6 months post-exposure
Tests for hepatitis B and C

fact_text: For occupational HIV exposure, PEP regimen depends on risk level: no PEP for no risk; AZT 300 mg + 3TC 150 mg twice daily for 28 days for low risk; AZT 300 mg + 3TC 150 mg twice daily plus LPV/r 200 mg/50 mg two tablets twice daily for 28 days for high risk.
