source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Moderate acute malnutrition (MAM) is defined as MUAC between 115 mm and less than 125 mm without oedema in children aged 6-59 months.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Severe acute malnutrition (SAM) is defined as MUAC less than 115 mm and/or presence of bipedal oedema in children aged 6-59 months.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Active case finding in the community using rapid screening methods such as MUAC measurement is essential to identify children with SAM early before complications develop.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: A combined approach is recommended: community-based management for SAM without complications and post-discharge care, and facility-based inpatient management for SAM with complications to optimize resource use and maximize coverage.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Until community-based care is established, all children with severe acute malnutrition (SAM) must be treated through facility-based care in a health facility to ensure treatment and reduce default rates.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: The National Guidelines are intended for doctors, senior nurses, and senior health professionals responsible for inpatient therapeutic care of children with SAM in health facilities in Bangladesh, adapted from WHO global guidelines.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: The guidelines include the complete protocol for management of SAM where community-based management is unavailable, covering: assessment and admission criteria, the '10 Steps' general management principles, treatment of associated conditions, management of treatment failure, discharge guidelines before full recovery, and emergency treatment of shock, anemia, severe pneumonia, and heart failure.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Bangladesh uses the WHO Growth Reference Standards (GRS) for determining WLZ/WHZ in children, as adopted nationally.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
admission_criteria: MUAC < 115 mm
WLZ/WHZ < -3
Bilateral pedal oedema
fact_text: A child aged 6-59 months is classified as having severe acute malnutrition (SAM) if they have one or more of the following: mid-upper arm circumference (MUAC) less than 115 mm, weight-for-length z-score (WLZ) or weight-for-height z-score (WHZ) less than -3, or presence of bilateral pedal oedema.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
admission_criteria: WLZ < -3
Bilateral pedal oedema
Visible wasting
contraindications_or_cautions: WLZ calculation not possible if length < 45 cm
fact_text: For infants under 6 months, SAM classification is uncertain; until better data is available, classify as SAM if the infant has one or more of: WLZ less than -3, bilateral pedal oedema, or visible wasting. If length is less than 45 cm, WLZ calculation is not possible.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Caregiver request for inpatient care is a criterion for admission to inpatient treatment.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: In areas with only facility-based inpatient care, all children meeting SAM criteria should be admitted to inpatient care.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Where both facility-based and community-based care are available, children with SAM without medical complications should be treated in community-based care.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition in infants under 6 months
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition in infants under 6 months
fact_text: Infants under 6 months with severe acute malnutrition require inpatient treatment.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with abnormal temperature
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with abnormal temperature
fact_text: Fever >39°C (102.2°F) axillary or hypothermia <35°C (95°F) axillary requires inpatient treatment in SAM children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with altered consciousness
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with altered consciousness
fact_text: Very weak, apathetic, unconscious, or fitting/convulsing children with SAM require inpatient treatment.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Severe anaemia defined as severely pale (severe palmer pallor) with or without difficulty breathing requires inpatient treatment in SAM children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Presence of Grade ++ or Grade +++ oedema requires inpatient treatment.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Dehydration based on recent history of diarrhoea, vomiting, fever or sweating, no urine for last 12 hours, and recent clinical signs of dehydration reported by caregiver requires inpatient treatment in SAM children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Extensive infection requiring parenteral treatment is an indication for inpatient treatment in SAM children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with medical complications
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with medical complications
fact_text: Children with SAM and medical complications should be admitted to facility-based inpatient therapeutic care until complications are controlled.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with oedema and wasting
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with oedema and wasting
fact_text: Any grade of oedema with MUAC <115 mm and/or WLZ or WHZ < -3 requires inpatient treatment.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with poor appetite
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with poor appetite
fact_text: Poor appetite or inability to eat is a criterion for inpatient treatment in SAM children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with rapid breathing
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with rapid breathing
fact_text: Rapid breathing defined as ≥60/min for children <2 months, ≥50/min for children 2-12 months, and ≥40/min for children 12-59 months requires inpatient treatment in SAM children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Persistent vomiting defined as vomiting 3 or more times per hour is an indication for inpatient treatment in SAM children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Oedema in children is graded as Grade + (mild: both feet/ankles), Grade ++ (moderate: both feet plus lower legs, hands or lower arms), and Grade +++ (severe: generalized oedema including feet, legs, hands, arms and face).

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
admission_criteria: Facility-based inpatient care for children with SAM and complications includes first seven management steps
followup_monitoring: After 4 to 7 days of inpatient care, child is referred to community-based care for continued management
fact_text: Management of children with severe acute malnutrition in facility-based inpatient care includes ten essential steps, with the first seven steps (treat/prevent hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, infection, micronutrient deficiencies, and cautious feeding including breastfeeding) completed over 4 to 7 days before referral to community-based care for continuation.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: The ten essential management steps for SAM are divided into two phases: (1) Stabilisation phase, addressing life-threatening problems, correcting deficiencies and metabolic abnormalities, and initiating feeding; (2) Rehabilitation phase, focusing on intensive feeding to recover lost weight, increasing emotional and physical stimulation, re-initiating or encouraging breastfeeding, training caregivers for home care, and preparing for discharge.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Hypoglycaemia in SAM is suspected if hypothermia (axillary temperature <35°C or <95°F), lethargy, limpness, convulsions, or loss of consciousness are present, or if the child has been fasting for 4-6 hours. Blood glucose <3 mmol/L (54 mg/dL) confirms hypoglycaemia. All children with SAM should be assumed hypoglycaemic and treated accordingly.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If the child with SAM is conscious and hypoglycaemic, give a 50 ml bolus of 10% glucose or sucrose solution orally or via nasogastric tube (equivalent to 5 g sugar in 50 ml or 1 rounded teaspoon sugar in 50 ml or 3.5 tablespoons water). Then feed starter diet F-75 every 30 minutes for 2 hours, providing one fourth of the total recommended two-hour feed volume each time. Keep the child warm, give antibiotics as per infection protocol, and continue two-hourly feeds day and night.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Table 1: Time-frame for the management of a child with severe acute malnutrition
fact_text: Management of SAM is divided into phases: Stabilization (days 1-2 and days 3-7) and Rehabilitation (weeks 2-6). Hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, and dehydration are addressed in days 1-2. Electrolyte correction starts day 3 and continues through rehabilitation. Infection treatment begins day 3 and continues. Micronutrients are given without iron during stabilization and with iron during rehabilitation. Cautious feeding occurs during stabilization (days 1-7). Catch-up growth and sensory stimulation start from day 3 and continue through rehabilitation. Preparation for follow-up begins during rehabilitation.
source_figure_or_table: Table 1: Time-frame for the management of a child with severe acute malnutrition

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Prevent hypoglycaemia and hypothermia by feeding every two hours and ensuring feeds throughout day and night.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Hypothermia is diagnosed if axillary temperature is below 35°C (95°F).

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: After initial treatment of hypoglycaemia, repeat blood glucose test after 2 hours; if blood glucose falls below 3 mmol/L, give a further 50 ml bolus of 10% glucose or sucrose and continue feeding every 30 minutes for 2 hours with one fourth of total recommended feed volume per feed.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If axillary temperature falls below 36.0°C (96.8°F), repeat blood glucose testing (dextrostix).

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If level of consciousness remains static despite treatment of hypoglycaemia, repeat hypoglycaemia treatment; if no improvement, consider other causes and refer to higher facility if possible.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If convulsions persist after IV glucose, give rectal diazepam at 0.5 mg/kg body weight.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Treat hypothermia by re-warming the child: clothe including head, cover with warmed blanket, increase ambient temperature with safe heat sources, or use Kangaroo Mother Care (skin-to-skin contact on mother's bare chest) and cover the child; feed as per Step 7 protocol.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Feed unconscious or convulsing children every two hours day and night as per Step 7 feeding protocol.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Administer antibiotics as per Step 5 protocol in unconscious or convulsing children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: For unconscious or convulsing children with SAM, give 10% glucose 5 ml/kg IV followed by 50 ml of 10% glucose or sucrose via NG tube, then start F-75 feeding as per protocol.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Feed the child every two hours starting immediately and continue feeds throughout day and night during stabilization, especially for the first 24-48 hours.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Avoid exposure such as bathing or prolonged medical examinations to prevent hypothermia in children with SAM.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Avoid regular bathing, keep the child dry, change wet nappies, clothes, and bedding to prevent hypothermia.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Prevent hypothermia by keeping the child covered at all times, especially at night, feeling for warmth, and letting the child sleep with mother or caregiver at night.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: In children with SAM, clinical signs of dehydration may be masked or confused by signs of malnutrition or septic shock; therefore, assume dehydration in any child with watery diarrhoea.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Check blood glucose level for hypoglycaemia whenever hypothermia is detected in a child with severe acute malnutrition.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: During re-warming of a hypothermic child, measure axillary temperature every 2 hours until temperature rises above 37.0°C or 98.6°F.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: ReSoMal recipe for SAM children: Water (boiled & cooled) 850 ml, WHO-ORS (new formulation) one 500 ml packet, Sugar 20 g, Electrolyte/mineral mix solution 16.6 ml (if available).

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Do not use standard ORS (90 mmol sodium/L) or newly modified WHO-ORS (75 mmol sodium/L) for children with SAM due to excess sodium and insufficient potassium; instead, use special Rehydration Solution for Malnutrition (ReSoMal).

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Monitor rehydration progress by observing pulse rate, respiratory rate, urine frequency, and stool/vomit frequency every 30 minutes for 2 hours, then hourly for 4-10 hours.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Persistent rapid breathing and rapid pulse during rehydration may indicate coexisting infection or overhydration.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Signs of progressing rehydration include slowing of rapid respiration and pulse rates, beginning to pass urine, return of tears, moist mouth, eyes and fontanelle appearing less sunken, improved skin turgor, and urination.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Do not use intravenous fluids for rehydration in children with oedema except in cases of shock; if IV fluids are used, infuse slowly to avoid fluid overload and heart failure.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Stop fluids immediately if any signs of overhydration occur, especially signs of heart failure, including increasing pulse rate by 25 beats/min or more, increasing respiratory rate by 5 breaths/min or more, or puffy eyelids/increasing oedema; reassess after one hour.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: After the initial 2 hours, give ReSoMal at 5-10 ml/kg/hour by alternate hours for 4-10 hours, adjusting the exact volume based on the child's demand, stool loss, and vomiting; continue F-75 feeding in alternate hours during this period until rehydration is achieved.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: For children with watery diarrhoea, give ReSoMal 5 ml/kg orally or via nasogastric tube every 30 minutes for the first 2 hours.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: watery diarrhoea with severe sodium loss
condition_aliases: watery diarrhoea with severe sodium loss
fact_text: If diarrhoea is severe with high sodium loss and risk of symptomatic hyponatraemia, use new WHO-ORS (75 mmol sodium/L) instead of ReSoMal for rehydration.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: dehydration in sam with continuing watery diarrhoea
condition_aliases: dehydration in sam with continuing watery diarrhoea
fact_text: To prevent dehydration in a child with continuing watery diarrhoea, keep feeding with starter F-75 as per Step 7, replace stool losses with ReSoMal at 5-10 ml/kg after each watery stool, and encourage continued breastfeeding with increased frequency if the child is breastfed.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: dehydration in sam with watery diarrhoea
condition_aliases: dehydration in sam with watery diarrhoea
fact_text: Stop ReSoMal as soon as the child shows 3 or more signs of improved hydration: no longer thirsty, passing urine, slowing of respiratory and pulse rates from previous high rates, skin pinch less slow, and presence of tears.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: All children with SAM have excess body sodium despite low plasma sodium; potassium and magnesium deficiencies are common and may take at least two weeks to correct; oedema is partly due to these imbalances.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: sam with electrolyte imbalance during feeding
condition_aliases: sam with electrolyte imbalance during feeding
fact_text: Prepare food without added salt for children with SAM during stabilization to correct electrolyte imbalance.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: sam with electrolyte imbalance during rehydration
condition_aliases: sam with electrolyte imbalance during rehydration
fact_text: When rehydrating children with SAM, use low sodium rehydration fluid such as ReSoMal.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: sam with electrolyte imbalance during stabilization
condition_aliases: sam with electrolyte imbalance during stabilization
fact_text: Until stabilization, give extra magnesium sulphate at 0.1 ml/kg/day for 1 week to children with SAM.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: sam with electrolyte imbalance during stabilization
condition_aliases: sam with electrolyte imbalance during stabilization
fact_text: Until stabilization, give extra potassium at 4 mmol/kg/day for 1 week to children with SAM.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Do NOT treat oedema in SAM with diuretics.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: All children with severe acute malnutrition have vitamin and mineral deficiencies; iron should NOT be given during the acute phase as it may worsen infections and anaemia is common; iron should be started only after infection is controlled, the child has good appetite, and begins to gain weight, usually by the second week.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: In severe acute malnutrition, usual signs of infection such as fever are often absent and infections are frequently hidden; therefore, all children with SAM should be routinely treated on admission with broad-spectrum antibiotics.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with clinical deterioration or septic shock or meningitis
condition_aliases: sam with septic shock or meningitis
severe acute malnutrition with clinical deterioration or septic shock or meningitis
dose_or_duration: Ceftriaxone 75-100 mg/kg once daily
fact_text: If the child with SAM fails to improve clinically by 48 hours or deteriorates after 24 hours, or presents with septic shock or meningitis, consider broader spectrum antibiotics such as ceftriaxone 75-100 mg/kg/day IV or IM once daily along with gentamicin.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with gentamicin treatment
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with gentamicin treatment
contraindications_or_cautions: avoid gentamicin if anuric or oliguria present
fact_text: Gentamicin may accumulate and cause deafness if the child is not passing urine; do not give the second dose of gentamicin until the child has passed urine.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with hiv exposure or infection
condition_aliases: sam with hiv exposure or infection
severe acute malnutrition with hiv exposure or infection
dose_or_duration: Trimethoprim 5 mg/kg/day
fact_text: If the child with SAM is HIV exposed or infected, provide co-trimoxazole prophylaxis at trimethoprim 5 mg/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia
dose_or_duration: Trimethoprim 20 mg/kg/day in 4 divided doses for 2 weeks
fact_text: If Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia is present in a child with SAM, treat with co-trimoxazole at trimethoprim 20 mg/kg/day divided into 4 doses for 2 weeks.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with severe illness or complications
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with severe illness or complications
dose_or_duration: Ampicillin 50 mg/kg every 6 hours for 2 days; then amoxicillin 15 mg/kg every 8 hours for 5 days; gentamicin 7.5 mg/kg once daily for 7 days
route_or_site: Ampicillin IM/IV; amoxicillin oral; gentamicin IM/IV
duration: Ampicillin 2 days; amoxicillin 5 days; gentamicin 7 days
fact_text: If the child with SAM is severely ill (apathetic, lethargic, or looking sick) or has complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw or broken skin, respiratory or urinary tract infection, lethargic/sickly appearance), give ampicillin 50 mg/kg IM or IV every 6 hours for 2 days, then oral amoxicillin 15 mg/kg every 8 hours for 5 days, plus gentamicin 7.5 mg/kg IM or IV once daily for 7 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with suspected malaria
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with suspected malaria
fact_text: If malaria is suspected in a child with SAM, anti-malarial treatment should be given.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition without signs of infection
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition without signs of infection
dose_or_duration: 15 mg/kg per dose, every 8 hours, for 5 days
fact_text: If the child with SAM appears to have no signs of infection or complications, give oral amoxicillin 15 mg/kg every 8 hours for 5 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: In the stabilisation phase, start feeding cautiously as soon as possible after admission to provide just sufficient energy and protein to maintain basic physiological processes; this applies to children aged 6-59 months; for infants under 6 months see Annex 9.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Give daily for at least 2 weeks: multivitamin supplement without iron, folic acid 1 mg/day (5 mg on Day 1), zinc 2 mg/kg/day, copper 0.3 mg/kg/day if available, and elemental iron 3 mg/kg/day only when child starts gaining weight (rehabilitation phase).

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Give vitamin A orally on Day 1 unless a dose was given in the last month; dose by age: >12 months 200,000 IU, 6-12 months 100,000 IU, 0-5 months 50,000 IU.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If combined electrolyte-mineral solution or combined mineral solution not available, give vitamin A on day 1, daily multivitamin, folic acid 1 mg/d (5 mg on Day 1), zinc 2 mg/kg/d, copper 0.3 mg/kg/d, elemental iron 3 mg/kg/d when gaining weight, potassium 4 mmol/kg/d for 1 week, and magnesium sulphate 0.1 ml/kg/day IM for 7 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: When combined electrolyte/mineral solution is available, give vitamin A on day 1, daily multivitamin, folic acid 1 mg/d (5 mg on Day 1), elemental iron 3 mg/kg/d when gaining weight, but do not give zinc or copper separately.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: During feeding, monitor amounts offered and left over, frequency of vomiting, frequency of watery stool, and daily body weight.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: During the stabilization phase, feeds should be small, frequent, low osmolarity, low lactose, with energy intake about 100 kcal/kg/day and protein intake 1-1.5 g/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: F-75 feeding schedule: Days 1-2: feed every 2 hours, 11 ml/kg/feed, total 130 ml/kg/day; Days 3-5: feed every 3 hours, 16 ml/kg/feed, total 130 ml/kg/day; Day 6 and beyond: feed every 4 hours, 22 ml/kg/feed, total 130 ml/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If the child is breastfed, breastfeeding should be encouraged alongside prescribed starter formula (F-75) to meet nutritional needs; re-lactation should be attempted in children under 24 months if feasible.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Total fluid intake from feeds should not exceed 130 ml/kg/day; reduce to 100 ml/kg/day if the child has severe (+++) oedema involving legs, hands, and face.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: For children with severe oedema, follow the severe oedema feeding chart; if energy intake is less than 80 kcal/kg/day, start nasogastric tube feeding; if breastfed, continue breastfeeding or attempt re-lactation with breastmilk supplementer if not breastfeeding and under 24 months.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If vomiting or frequent loose stools (≥5/day) or poor appetite, continue 2-hourly F-75 feeds; if little or no vomiting, less frequent loose stools (<5/day), and finishing most feeds, change to 3-hourly feeds; after one day on 3-hourly feeds with no vomiting, less diarrhoea, and finishing most feeds, change to 4-hourly feeds.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: During the transition from F-75 to F-100 feeding, monitor for signs of heart failure by regularly assessing respiratory rate and pulse rate.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Caregivers must be motivated and spend sufficient time with the child to ensure completion of each feed; children should be encouraged to eat actively while sitting comfortably on the caregiver's lap and must never be left to eat alone.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: In the rehabilitation phase for children aged 6-59 months with SAM, vigorous feeding is required to achieve rapid weight gain >10 g/kg/day, signaled by return of appetite about one week after admission and loss of most or all oedema.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: The recommended milk-based catch-up formula F-100 contains 100 kcal and 2.9 g protein per 100 ml; during later rehabilitation phase, gradual replacement of F-100 with family foods like khichuri or halwa containing equivalent kilocalories is advised.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: To transition from starter formula F-75 to catch-up formula F-100, replace F-75 with equal volume of F-100 every 4 hours for 48 hours (transitional phase), then increase each feed by 10 ml until some feed remains uneaten, typically when intake reaches about 30 ml/kg/feed or 200 ml/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Interpret weight gain after transition as: poor if <5 g/kg/day requiring full reassessment; moderate if 5-10 g/kg/day requiring review of intake and infection; good if >10 g/kg/day to continue current care.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Monitor progress after transition by weighing the child each morning before feeding and plotting weight on a graph to assess rate of weight gain.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Weight gain in g/kg/day is calculated as ((W2 - W1) x 1000) / (W1 x number of days between W1 and W2), where W1 is initial or lowest weight in kg and W2 is weight on day of calculation; daily weight gain averages can be used if weights are taken daily.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: During early rehabilitation, children with oedema may not gain weight despite adequate intake due to oedema fluid loss; progress is assessed by decreased oedema rather than weight gain.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If child is neither gaining weight nor showing decreased oedema, or oedema is increasing, reassess management and look for pitfalls or complications.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: After transition phase, provide frequent feeds at least every 4 hours of unlimited catch-up formula F-100 to achieve energy intake of 150-220 kcal/kg/day and protein intake of 4-6 g/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If the child is breastfed, encourage continued breastfeeding during catch-up feeding, but note breast milk alone is insufficient to support rapid catch-up growth in SAM children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Provide sensory stimulation and emotional support to children with severe malnutrition including tender loving care (smiling, laughing, patting, touching), a cheerful stimulating environment, structured play therapy 15-30 minutes daily using locally available low-cost toys, physical activity as soon as the child is well enough, and parental/caregiver involvement to continue special care at home.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: A child who has achieved WLZ or WHZ ≥ -2 can be considered recovered and eligible for discharge from hospital, but follow-up is essential to prevent relapse.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Criteria for discharge from inpatient care in areas where there is no community-based outpatient care
fact_text: Discharge criteria from inpatient care in areas without community-based outpatient care: Child must have WHZ ≥ -2, resolved oedema, no infections or medical complications, and completed or planned immunization.
source_figure_or_table: Criteria for discharge from inpatient care in areas where there is no community-based outpatient care

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Criteria for discharge from inpatient care in areas where there is no community-based outpatient care
fact_text: Mother/caregiver discharge criteria: must know how to prepare a homemade balanced diet and feed the child, give home treatment for diarrhoea, recognize danger signs for seeking medical assistance, and receive advice for follow-up.
source_figure_or_table: Criteria for discharge from inpatient care in areas where there is no community-based outpatient care

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Parents should be taught to understand causes of malnutrition and prevention including correct breastfeeding and feeding practices with frequent energy and nutrient dense foods, how to treat or seek treatment for diarrhoea and infections, timing of immunizations, ensuring vitamin A supplementation for children aged 6-59 months and anthelmintic drugs for children aged 24-59 months every 6 months, and how to provide structured play therapy to the child.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Children discharged after SAM treatment should be enrolled in CMAM programme and attend monthly GMP sessions at health centers or NGO facilities up to 5 years of age.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Children discharged after SAM treatment should be enrolled in Safety Net programme for ongoing support.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Follow-up visits should occur at 1 week after discharge at treated health facility or nearby public/NGO facilities, then at 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, 3 months, and every 3 months thereafter until WHZ > 1 is achieved.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Children with vitamin A deficiency are likely photophobic with closed eyes; eyes should be examined gently to prevent damage or rupture.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: corneal clouding or ulceration in sam
condition_aliases: corneal clouding or ulceration in sam
fact_text: For corneal clouding or ulceration in SAM, instil chloramphenicol 1% eye drops every 2-3 hours for 7-10 days and tetracycline eye ointment at night; instil atropine 1% eye drops one drop three times daily for 3-5 days; cover eye with saline-soaked pads and bandage to prevent lens extrusion.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Signs of dermatosis in SAM include hypo- or hyperpigmentation, desquamation, ulceration over limbs/thighs/genitalia/groin/behind ears, and exudative lesions often with secondary Candida infection.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Zinc deficiency is common in children with dermatosis in SAM; zinc supplementation at 1-2 mg/kg/day for 2 weeks improves skin condition.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Alternatively, treat helminthiasis in SAM with mebendazole 100 mg twice daily for 3 days for children aged ≥24 months; not recommended below 24 months.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Alternatively, treat helminthiasis in SAM with pyrantel pamoate 10 mg/kg single dose for any age.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Treatment of helminth infections in SAM should be delayed until rehabilitation phase; give a single dose of 200 mg albendazole for children aged 12-23 months, 400 mg albendazole for children aged ≥24 months.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: vitamin a deficiency prevention in sam
condition_aliases: vitamin a deficiency prevention in sam
fact_text: Vitamin A dosing for children with SAM: 50,000 IU on days 1, 2, and 14 for children 0-6 months; 100,000 IU for children 6-12 months; 200,000 IU for children ≥12 months. If first dose given at referring center, treat only on days 1 and 14.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: For weeping skin lesions in kwashiorkor, keep perineum dry; apply gauze soaked in 1% potassium permanganate solution over affected areas for 10 minutes twice daily; treat candidiasis with clotrimazole cream twice daily for 2 weeks and oral nystatin 100,000 IU four times daily for oral candidiasis.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: other infections and associated conditions in sam
condition_aliases: other infections and associated conditions in sam
recommended_advice: Treat other associated infections and conditions according to national guidelines
fact_text: Treat other infections and associated conditions in children with SAM according to the national guidelines of Bangladesh.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
trigger_evidence: chest infection not responding to antibiotics
recommended_tests: Mantoux test (induration >5 mm after 48 hours considered positive)
fact_text: In SAM children with strong suspicion of tuberculosis (contact with TB patient, poor growth despite intake, chronic cough >2 weeks, or chest infection unresponsive to antibiotics), perform Mantoux test (induration >5 mm after 48 hours positive) and chest X-ray if possible; note Mantoux false negatives are common in severe malnutrition; treat according to National TB Control Guidelines if positive or strong suspicion.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
recommended_medicines: metronidazole 7.5 mg/kg every 8 hours for 7 days for giardiasis
ciprofloxacin 10 mg/kg every 12 hours for 3 days for bloody diarrhoea
pivmecillinam 15 mg/kg every 6 hours for 5 days for bloody diarrhoea
dose_or_duration: metronidazole 7.5 mg/kg 8-hourly for 7 days; ciprofloxacin 10 mg/kg 12-hourly for 3 days; pivmecillinam 15 mg/kg 6-hourly for 5 days
fact_text: In children with continuing diarrhoea during SAM treatment, stool microscopy should be done if possible; treat giardiasis with oral metronidazole 7.5 mg/kg every 8 hours for 7 days; if stool contains visible blood, treat with oral ciprofloxacin 10 mg/kg every 12 hours for 3 days or pivmecillinam 15 mg/kg every 6 hours for 5 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition_aliases: osmotic diarrhoea due to lactose intolerance
recommended_advice: substitute animal milk with yoghurt or lactose-free infant formula such as rice suji
reintroduce milk feeds gradually during rehabilitation phase
fact_text: If continuing diarrhoea is suspected to be due to lactose intolerance and is preventing improvement, substitute animal milk with yoghurt or lactose-free infant formula (e.g., rice suji) and reintroduce milk feeds gradually during the rehabilitation phase.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: osmotic diarrhoea suspected from f-75 with milk powder
condition_aliases: osmotic diarrhoea suspected from f-75 with milk powder
trigger_evidence: worsening diarrhoea after F-75 with milk powder
recommended_advice: use low osmolar cereal-based F-75 or yoghurt or rice suji instead of milk powder F-75
introduce F-100 gradually
fact_text: If diarrhoea worsens substantially in young children after F-75 prepared with milk powder, suspect osmotic diarrhoea and use low osmolar cereal-based F-75 or yoghurt or rice suji, then introduce F-100 gradually.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Case fatality rates (CFR) for children with SAM are categorized as unacceptable if >20%, poor if 11-20%, moderate if 5-10%, and good if <5%.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If mortality exceeds 5%, investigate timing and cause of deaths: within 24 hours consider untreated or delayed treatment of hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, septicaemia, severe anaemia, or incorrect rehydration fluid/volume or IV fluid overuse; within 72 hours check for excessive feed volume, wrong feed formulation, potassium deficiency, or incorrect antibiotics; at night consider hypothermia from insufficient covers or no night feeds; when changing to catch-up F-100 consider too rapid transition; after 7 days consider hospital-acquired sepsis.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: For inadequate feeding as a cause of poor weight gain, check that night feeds are given; target energy and protein intake calculations are correct; actual intake is recorded accurately; feeding technique ensures frequent feeding with unlimited amounts; quality of care is motivated, gentle, and loving; feed preparation includes weighing, measuring, hygienic preparation, and proper mixing; and family foods are suitably modified to provide >100 kcal/100g or re-modified if not.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: For specific nutrient deficiencies as a cause of poor weight gain, check adequacy of multivitamin composition and shelf-life.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If weight gain is less than 5 g/kg/day during rehabilitation, determine if this applies to all cases (indicating need for major Nutrition Unit management overhaul) or specific cases requiring reassessment including screening for infections such as tuberculosis, urinary tract infection, and ear infection.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Low weight gain during the rehabilitation phase is categorized as poor if <5 g/kg/day, moderate if 5-10 g/kg/day, and good if >10 g/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Possible causes of poor weight gain include inadequate feeding and specific nutrient deficiencies.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Children with HIV/AIDS may have slower recovery and more treatment failures; gut enteropathy is worse and often caused by Cryptosporidium parvum; lactose intolerance is common in severe HIV-related chronic diarrhoea; children with monosaccharide and disaccharide intolerance may benefit from lactose-free preparations.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Alter antibiotic schedule only if a specific infection is identified after investigations.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Check for abnormal behaviours such as stereotyped movements (rocking), rumination (self-stimulation through regurgitation), and attention seeking; ensure extra care, love, and attention.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: In suspected hidden infection with adequate feeding and no malabsorption, re-examine temperature, pulse, and respiration every 3 hours; repeat urinalysis for white blood cells; examine stools for intestinal infections and blood; take chest X-ray if possible; test blood for dengue, hepatitis B, and malaria.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
recommended_advice: Train caregiver on feeding and structured play
Ensure caregiver motivation and support
Plan for weekly visits and easy hospital access
fact_text: For safe discharge, the mother/caregiver must not be employed outside the home, be specifically trained on appropriate feeding (type, amount, frequency), have financial resources to feed the child, live within easy reach of the hospital for urgent readmission, be visitable weekly, be trained to provide structured play therapy, and be motivated to follow advice.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: A child with SAM may be considered recovered and ready for discharge when reaching 80% WHZ or higher; earlier discharge is possible if effective alternative supervision is available and specific criteria are met.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: For discharge readiness, the child must be older than 12 months, have lost oedema, completed antibiotic treatment, show good appetite and weight gain, and have taken potassium, magnesium, mineral, and vitamin supplements for at least 2 weeks or be continuing supplementation at home.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Local health workers are trained to support home care, including clinical examination at home, deciding referral timing, weighing the child, and providing appropriate advice.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: A practical approach for home feeding during SAM rehabilitation is to use simple modifications of usual home foods, such as preparing Khichuri with home foods.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: During home rehabilitation of children with SAM, frequent meals with high energy and protein content should be given, providing at least 150 kcal/kg/day and at least 4 g protein/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Feeding frequency at home rehabilitation should be at least 5 times per day with foods containing approximately 100 kcal and 2-3 g protein per 100 g.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: During home rehabilitation, vitamins, iron, and electrolyte-mineral supplements can be continued.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: shock in children with severe acute malnutrition
condition_aliases: shock in children with severe acute malnutrition
fact_text: Diagnosis of shock in children with severe acute malnutrition requires lethargy or unconsciousness, cold hands, plus either slow capillary refill (>3 seconds) or weak/fast pulse (≥160/min for 2-12 months, ≥140/min for 1-5 years).

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: shock in children with severe acute malnutrition
condition_aliases: shock in children with severe acute malnutrition
fact_text: Signs suggesting septic shock include signs of dehydration without watery diarrhoea history, hypothermia or hypoglycaemia, and poor response to IV fluids compared to dehydration where IV fluids elicit response.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: shock in children with severe acute malnutrition
condition_aliases: shock in children with severe acute malnutrition
fact_text: Fluid volume for shock treatment in children with severe acute malnutrition should be determined by the child's response, with strict avoidance of overhydration.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition_aliases: shock due to acute watery diarrhoea
fact_text: Initial shock treatment includes giving oxygen, IV 10% glucose 5 ml/kg, IV fluids at 20 ml/kg over 1 hour using Ringer's lactate with 5% dextrose or half-strength normal saline with 5% dextrose or cholera saline or half-strength Darrow's solution with 5% dextrose, measuring pulse and respiration every 30 minutes, giving antibiotics, and keeping the child warm.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: shock due to acute watery diarrhoea
condition_aliases: shock due to acute watery diarrhoea
fact_text: If shock is due to acute watery diarrhoea, use cholera saline at 20 ml/kg/hour for the first 2 hours.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition_aliases: pulse and respiration rates remain high
fact_text: If the child fails to improve (pulse and respiration rates remain high), assume septic shock: give maintenance IV fluids at 3 ml/kg/hour while waiting for blood, transfuse fresh whole blood at 10 ml/kg slowly over 3 hours when available, and treat sepsis with antibiotics.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If signs of improvement occur (pulse and respiration rates fall), repeat IV fluids at 15 ml/kg over 1 hour, then switch to oral or nasogastric rehydration with ReSoMal at 10 ml/kg/hour in alternate hours with starter F-75 for up to 10 hours, then continue feeding with starter F-75.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If signs of over-hydration occur during treatment, defined as breathing increasing by 5 or more breaths per minute and pulse increasing by 25 or more beats per minute, stop the infusion to prevent worsening of the child's condition.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Blood transfusion is required if haemoglobin is less than 5 g/dL or packed cell volume is less than 15%, or if breathlessness is present with haemoglobin between 5 and 7 g/dL.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Monitor for transfusion reactions during blood transfusion and stop transfusion if fever, itchy rash, dark red urine, confusion, or shock develop.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Monitor respiratory rate and pulse rate every 15 minutes during transfusion; if either rises, transfuse more slowly.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: anaemia (mild, moderate, severe) in malnourished children
condition_aliases: anaemia (mild, moderate, severe) in malnourished children
fact_text: Oral elemental iron at 3 mg/kg/day should be given for at least three months to replenish iron stores in all anaemia cases, but only after the child has begun to gain weight.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Management of heart failure includes propped up position, oxygen, stopping or slowing IV fluids or transfusion, IV furosemide 1-3 mg/kg STAT slowly, digoxin 5 micrograms/kg single dose IV or orally if needed, and if heart failure is due to severe anaemia, transfuse 5-7 ml/kg packed cells.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Administer whole blood transfusion at 10 ml/kg body weight slowly over 3 hours for severe anaemia in malnourished children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Give furosemide 1 mg/kg intravenously at the start of the blood transfusion for severe anaemia in malnourished children.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe anaemia in malnourished children with cardiac failure
condition_aliases: severe anaemia in malnourished children with cardiac failure
fact_text: For severely anaemic children with signs of cardiac failure, transfuse packed cells at 5-7 ml/kg instead of whole blood.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Simplified field tables - Weight-for-length Birth to 2 years (z-scores)
fact_text: Weight-for-length z-score reference values for boys and girls from birth to 2 years are provided, with severe acute malnutrition defined as weight-for-length z-score below -3 SD according to WHO Child Growth Standards.
source_figure_or_table: Simplified field tables - Weight-for-length Birth to 2 years (z-scores)

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Electrolyte-mineral solution for ReSoMal is prepared by weighing and mixing 224 g potassium chloride (KCl), 81 g tripotassium citrate (C6H5K3O7.H2O), 76 g magnesium chloride (MgCl2.6H2O), 8.2 g zinc acetate (Zn(CH3COO)2.2H2O), and 1.4 g copper sulphate (CuSO4.5H2O), then making up to 2500 ml with water; 20 ml of this solution is added to 1000 ml of milk feed.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
dose_or_duration: 20 ml
fact_text: Electrolyte-mineral solution molar contents per 20 ml dose: potassium chloride 24 mmol, tripotassium citrate 2 mmol, magnesium chloride 3 mmol, zinc acetate 300 micromol, copper sulphate 45 micromol.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: ReSoMal oral rehydration solution recipe table
fact_text: ReSoMal oral rehydration solution is prepared by mixing 850 ml boiled and cooled water, one 500 ml packet of WHO-ORS (new formulation), 20 g sugar, and 16.5 ml of electrolyte-mineral solution for oral rehydration in children with SAM.
source_figure_or_table: ReSoMal oral rehydration solution recipe table

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: If electrolyte-mineral solution premixed sachets are unavailable, potassium should be given as a 10% stock solution of potassium chloride (100 g KCl in 1 litre water); for oral rehydration solution, use 40 ml of this stock instead of 33 ml electrolyte-mineral solution; for milk feeds, add 22.5 ml of stock instead of 20 ml electrolyte-mineral solution; if KCl is unavailable, give syrup potassium at 4 mmol/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Magnesium should be given as 50% magnesium sulphate intramuscularly once at 0.3 ml/kg up to a maximum of 2 ml.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Electrolyte-mineral solution should be prepared by dissolving ingredients in cooled boiled water, stored in sterilized bottles in the fridge to retard deterioration, discarded if cloudy, and freshly made each month.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: Zinc should be given at a dose of 2 mg/kg/day.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw skin/fissures, respiratory tract infections, or lethargic/sickly appearance)
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw skin/fissures, respiratory tract infections, or lethargic/sickly appearance)
fact_text: For children with SAM and complications, give ampicillin 50 mg/kg by IM or IV every 6 hours for 2 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw skin/fissures, respiratory tract infections, or lethargic/sickly appearance)
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw skin/fissures, respiratory tract infections, or lethargic/sickly appearance)
fact_text: For children with SAM and complications, give ceftriaxone 75-100 mg/kg daily by IM or IV for 5 to 7 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw skin/fissures, respiratory tract infections, or lethargic/sickly appearance)
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw skin/fissures, respiratory tract infections, or lethargic/sickly appearance)
fact_text: For children with SAM and complications, give gentamicin 7.5 mg/kg once daily by IM or IV for 7 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw skin/fissures, respiratory tract infections, or lethargic/sickly appearance)
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with complications (shock, hypoglycaemia, hypothermia, dermatosis with raw skin/fissures, respiratory tract infections, or lethargic/sickly appearance)
fact_text: For children with SAM and complications, give oral amoxicillin 15 mg/kg every 8 hours for 5 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
condition: severe acute malnutrition with specific infection requiring additional antibiotic
condition_aliases: severe acute malnutrition with specific infection requiring additional antibiotic
fact_text: If a specific infection requires an additional antibiotic in a child with SAM, give specific antibiotics as required.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: For children with severe acute malnutrition without complications, give oral amoxicillin 15 mg/kg every 8 hours for 5 days.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Doses for iron syrup for a common formulation
fact_text: Dose and amount of iron depend on the type of iron salt supplied: 200 mg ferrous fumerate contains 65 mg elemental iron; 200 mg ferrous sulphate contains 60 mg elemental iron.
source_figure_or_table: Doses for iron syrup for a common formulation

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Amoxicillin
fact_text: Amoxicillin oral dose is 15 mg/kg every 8 hours for 5 days; for 3.0-5.9 kg child use 1/4 tablet (250 mg) or 2.5 ml syrup (125 mg/5 ml) or 1.5 ml syrup (250 mg/5 ml); for 6.0-7.9 kg use 1/2 tablet or 5 ml syrup (125 mg/5 ml) or 2 ml syrup (250 mg/5 ml); for 8.0-9.9 kg use 1/2 tablet or 5 ml syrup (125 mg/5 ml) or 2.5 ml syrup (250 mg/5 ml).
source_figure_or_table: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Amoxicillin

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Ceftriaxone
fact_text: Ceftriaxone dose is 75-100 mg/kg/day by IM or IV once daily for 7 days; dose for 3 kg child is 2.25 ml, for 4 kg 3.00 ml, for 5 kg 3.75 ml, for 6 kg 4.50 ml, for 7 kg 5.25 ml, for 8 kg 6.00 ml, for 9 kg 6.75 ml, for 10 kg 7.50 ml, for 11 kg 8.25 ml, and for 12 kg 9.00 ml.
source_figure_or_table: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Ceftriaxone

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Gentamicin (80 mg vial diluted)
fact_text: Gentamicin dose for vial containing 80 mg (2 ml at 40 mg/ml) mixed with 6 ml sterile water to give 80 mg/8 ml, IV or IM once daily for 7 days: 3 kg 2.25 ml, 4 kg 3.00 ml, 5 kg 3.75 ml, 6 kg 4.50 ml, 7 kg 5.25 ml, 8 kg 6.00 ml, 9 kg 6.75 ml, 10 kg 7.50 ml, 11 kg 8.25 ml, 12 kg 9.00 ml.
source_figure_or_table: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Gentamicin (80 mg vial diluted)

source_section: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Gentamicin (80 mg vial undiluted)
fact_text: Gentamicin dose for vial containing 80 mg (2 ml at 40 mg/ml) undiluted, IV or IM once daily for 7 days: 3 kg 0.50 ml, 4 kg 0.75 ml, 5 kg 0.90 ml, 6 kg 1.10 ml, 7 kg 1.30 ml, 8 kg 1.50 ml, 9 kg 1.70 ml, 10 kg 1.90 ml, 11 kg 2.00 ml, 12 kg 2.25 ml.
source_figure_or_table: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Gentamicin (80 mg vial undiluted)

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Gentamicin (20 mg vial undiluted)
fact_text: Gentamicin dose is 7.5 mg/kg once daily IV or IM for 7 days; dose volume varies by vial formulation: for vial containing 20 mg (2 ml at 10 mg/ml) undiluted, dose for 3 kg is 2.25 ml, 4 kg 3.00 ml, 5 kg 3.75 ml, 6 kg 4.50 ml, 7 kg 5.25 ml, 8 kg 6.00 ml, 9 kg 6.75 ml, 10 kg 7.50 ml, 11 kg 8.25 ml, 12 kg 9.00 ml.
source_figure_or_table: Doses for specific formulations and bodyweight ranges - Gentamicin (20 mg vial undiluted)

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
source_section: Doses for iron syrup for a common formulation
fact_text: Iron syrup oral dose is 3 mg/kg daily; formulation is ferrous fumerate 100 mg/5 ml (20 mg elemental iron per ml); dose volume for 3.0-5.9 kg child is 0.5 ml, for 6.0-9.9 kg is 0.75 ml, and for 10.0-14.9 kg is 1 ml daily.

fact_text: The recipe for a nutritional feed includes 300 ml full-cream cow's milk (fresh or long life), 70 g sugar, 35 g cereal flour (locally available rice, wheat, maize, or other cereal), 20 g (or 20 ml) vegetable oil (e.g., soyabean oil), 20 ml electrolyte mineral mix, and water to make up to 1000 ml total volume.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: When preparing the nutritional feed using a hand whisk: mix flour, milk or milk powder, sugar, oil, and electrolyte/mineral mix in a 1-litre measuring jug. Slowly add cooled boiled water up to 1000 ml. Transfer to a cooking pot and whisk vigorously while boiling gently for 4 minutes. After cooking, transfer back to the measuring jug, add boiled water to make 1000 ml if needed, and whisk again.

source_title: National Guidelines for the Facility-based Management of Children with Severe Acute Malnutrition in Bangladesh, 2017
fact_text: When preparing the nutritional feed using an electric blender: first put about 200 ml boiled, cooled water into the blender (omit if using liquid milk instead of milk powder), then add flour, milk or milk powder, sugar, oil, and electrolyte/mineral solution and blend. Add cooled boiled water to reach 1000 ml and blend at high speed. Transfer to a cooking pot and boil gently for 4 minutes with continuous stirring. After cooking, transfer back to blender, add boiled water to make 1000 ml if needed, and blend again.

fact_text: New admission is defined as patient directly enrolled to nutrition unit to start treatment (B1,B2,B3,B4,B5). Transfer in is patient started treatment elsewhere and referred to continue treatment. Cured patient meets discharge criteria per national guidelines. Death must be confirmed by home visit for outpatients. Defaulter is absent for 2 consecutive weighings (2 days inpatient or 2 weeks outpatient). Non-responder is patient not reaching discharge criteria after 3 months (90 days) outpatient. Transfers out are patients referred to another facility to continue treatment. Total end of month = beginning + admissions - discharges.
