followup_monitoring: Supervisory visits should be planned meticulously with schedules prepared in advance and include review of previous supervisory findings and health facility information.
fact_text: Supervisory visits for TB control must be planned in advance, include review of previous findings, and aim to improve implementation, data validation, and staff support.
source_figure_or_table: TP supervision policy flowchart showing Central Level > Division > Upazila > Community

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Use supervisory checklists systematically during supervisory visits to review and identify administrative and technical issues related to TB program implementation.
followup_monitoring: Review trends of presumptive TB cases monthly and calculate presumptive TB notification rates by geographic area.
Review sputum positivity rates among presumptive TB cases and during follow-up examinations to identify causes of very low or very high positivity rates.
Review turnaround times for reporting and discuss identified issues.
Check quality and quantity of sputum samples and smears (size, shape, thickness, evenness, staining).
Check maintenance status of microscopes, Xpert machines, and other laboratory equipment.
Ensure adequate supply of laboratory consumables for at least one month.
Check infection control measures including patient waiting areas, sputum collection outside, mask availability and use.
fact_text: Supervisory visits should systematically review presumptive TB case trends, sputum positivity rates, sample quality, reporting turnaround, equipment maintenance, consumable supplies, and infection control measures to ensure quality TB diagnosis and management.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Review quarterly TB case notification trends including bacteriologically confirmed cases, retreatment cases, and all cases per defined population to identify unusual or inconsistent events and suggest remedial measures.
fact_text: Quarterly review of TB case notification trends (bacteriologically confirmed, retreatment, all cases) per defined population is recommended to detect unusual patterns and guide remedial actions.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Calculate sputum conversion rate after 2 months of treatment for new and previously treated bacteriologically confirmed TB cases as percentage becoming smear-negative; expected rate 85-90%. Investigate and provide feedback if rates are low or very high.
fact_text: Sputum conversion rate at 2 months for new and previously treated bacteriologically confirmed TB cases should be around 85-90%; deviations require investigation and feedback.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Unsuccessful treatment outcomes include lost to follow-up, failure, death, and transferred-out; calculate rates among new bacteriologically confirmed cases and similarly for previously treated, clinically diagnosed, and extra-pulmonary cases; analyze reasons and provide feedback.
fact_text: Unsuccessful outcomes (lost to follow-up, failure, death, transferred out) should be calculated and analyzed for new bacteriologically confirmed and other TB cases to identify causes and improve outcomes.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Health education and counselling should include checking availability and use of updated BCC materials, reviewing counselling procedures, interviewing patients randomly, relating findings with patient card data, and checking patient knowledge about disease, treatment duration, and consequences of interruption.
fact_text: Health education and counselling must ensure updated BCC materials are used, counselling procedures reviewed, patient interviews conducted, and patient knowledge about TB and treatment consequences assessed.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Supervision reports should be completed on-site with health personnel, submitted to relevant authorities, and feedback provided to field staff and officials to improve TB program performance.
fact_text: Supervision reports must be filled on-site with health staff, submitted to authorities, and feedback given to field staff to enhance TB program quality.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Calculate treatment success rate as percentage of new bacteriologically confirmed cases declared cured or treatment completed; also applicable to Xpert MTB/RIF positive, previously treated, clinically diagnosed, and extra-pulmonary cases. Treatment completion without cure declaration should not exceed 5%.
fact_text: Treatment success rate is calculated as cured or treatment completed cases among new bacteriologically confirmed TB cases; similar calculation applies to Xpert MTB/RIF positive, previously treated, clinically diagnosed, and EPTB cases.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
followup_monitoring: Evaluation is the periodic assessment of TB program activities to measure effectiveness and support informed decisions for future strategies.
Evaluation involves systematic recording and review of interventions and outcomes to determine if program targets are met and to guide improvements.
The National TB Program (NTP) advocates continuous internal monitoring and external joint evaluations every two to three years by national and international experts.
fact_text: Evaluation of TB programs includes periodic assessment of activities and outcomes, with internal monitoring and external joint evaluations every 2-3 years.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
followup_monitoring: Monitoring is the systematic ongoing collection, collation, analysis, and interpretation of data to detect deviations from expected norms and provide feedback for corrective actions in TB programs.
Monitoring includes routine report review focusing on data management, supply, finance, training, quality assurance, and drug use.
Supervisory visits reinforce routine reporting requirements and provide on-the-spot training and direct monitoring.
Sentinel reporting supplements routine reporting and is useful during rapid or substantial system changes to detect unexpected or unintended outcomes.
Monitoring and supervision are ongoing processes requiring regular plans at all levels.
fact_text: Monitoring in TB programs involves routine report review, supervisory visits, and sentinel reporting to ensure data quality and program performance.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Patients should carry the Tuberculosis Identity Card to all health facility visits to access TB-related services including follow-up and adverse drug reaction monitoring.
Patients should be advised to safely retain the identity card after treatment completion for future reference.
fact_text: Patients must carry and safely retain the Tuberculosis Identity Card for accessing TB services and future reference.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: A standardized recording and reporting system is essential for monitoring TB case detection, treatment outcomes, and program performance at all health system levels.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: The TB Treatment Card includes a special box for pediatric TB cases and drug doses of child TB, which must be updated if dosages change due to weight gain or loss during treatment.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: The Tuberculosis Identity Card (TB 02) is prepared by medical staff at diagnosis for each TB patient and must be safely retained by the patient; it records treatment initiation date and patient categorization.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: The original TB Treatment Card should be kept at the registering health facility, with a duplicate sent to the treatment centre; the card must be updated daily by the DOT provider to reflect medicine intake and during supervisory visits.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: The Tuberculosis Treatment Card (TB 01) must be issued and completed for every diagnosed TB patient, documenting patient details, diagnostic classification, treatment regimen, medicine doses, follow-up sputum results, body weight, HIV status, and medicine collection data.
fact_text: The Tuberculosis Treatment Card (TB 01) must be issued and completed for every diagnosed TB patient, documenting patient details, diagnostic classification, treatment regimen, medicine doses, follow-up sputum results, body weight, HIV status, and medicine collection data.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: At the end of each quarter, the TB Laboratory Register records: number of presumptive TB cases, total smears examined, smear-positive patients diagnosed, follow-up smears examined, and number of positives among follow-up smears; source of referral must be documented.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Request form (TB 05) for AFB microscopy/Xpert MTB/RIF must be filled by medical or relevant staff requesting the test; if smears are done onsite, the form accompanies the specimen; if done elsewhere, smears and form must be sent to the examining lab.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: The Tuberculosis Laboratory Register (TB 04) records all tests performed in TB labs, including sputum AFB and Xpert MTB/RIF, tracking presumptive TB cases examined, bacteriologically confirmed TB cases, follow-up smear results, and Xpert MTB/RIF positive cases; a serial number is assigned per patient annually.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: The Tuberculosis Register (TB 03) at treatment facilities records patient info, disease classification, treatment dates, diagnostic results (X-ray, microscopy, Xpert MTB/RIF, histopathology), and treatment outcomes; it must be updated regularly and compared with electronic registers for concordance.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Record detailed patient contact information including mobile phone number when sputum is sent for diagnosis to enable tracing if positive and patient does not return.
fact_text: Patient contact details must be recorded when sputum is sent for diagnosis to enable tracing if positive and patient does not return.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Tuberculosis referral/transfer form (TB 07) must be filled in triplicate for patient transfer between health facilities; copies go to receiving centre, patient, and remain in file.
referral_criteria: Use TB 07 form for referring or transferring patients between health facilities.
fact_text: TB 07 referral/transfer form must be completed in triplicate for patient transfer between health facilities.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Requisition form for drugs (TB 08) should be prepared quarterly based on calculated drug requirements from previous quarter cases and doses, ensuring minimum stock for at least one patient per category.
fact_text: TB 08 drug requisition form must be prepared quarterly using calculated drug requirements and stock to ensure adequate supply and avoid overstocking.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Absentee tracing form (TB 09) should be used to retrieve patients who miss scheduled drug intake.
followup_monitoring: Use TB 09 form for tracing patients lost to follow-up for drug intake.
fact_text: TB 09 absentee tracing form is used to retrieve patients who do not attend scheduled drug intake.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Form DR TB 06 must be fully completed and sent with samples or patient for diagnosis or follow-up of presumptive or confirmed DR TB cases, indicating reason for culture, DST, and Xpert MTB/RIF testing.
fact_text: Form DR TB 06 is mandatory for requesting lab tests for presumptive or treated DR TB cases and must indicate reason for culture, DST, and Xpert MTB/RIF testing.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Early morning sputum sample is preferred for Xpert MTB/RIF testing if available.
If Xpert MTB/RIF is not available, sputum should be transported to nearest facility with Xpert MTB/RIF.
fact_text: Early morning sputum sample is preferred for Xpert MTB/RIF testing; if unavailable, transport sputum to nearest Xpert MTB/RIF facility.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Quarterly report on treatment results (TB 11) is for cohort analysis of treatment outcomes for patients starting treatment 12-15 months earlier.
Treatment outcomes are evaluated separately by patient type and collected from updated Tuberculosis Register.
Report should be prepared similarly to case finding report.
fact_text: Quarterly treatment results report (TB 11) analyzes cohort treatment outcomes for patients starting treatment 12-15 months earlier, using updated Tuberculosis Register data, prepared similarly to case finding report.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Quarterly TB case finding report (TB 10) must identify all patients registered in the Tuberculosis Register during the quarter.
Count new smear-positive cases by sex and age group, enter in Block 1; similarly count Xpert MTB/RIF positive cases in Block 1.
Count smear-positive previously treated patients divided into relapse, treatment after failure, and treatment after lost to follow-up (LTFU).
Count smear-negative cases, extrapulmonary TB cases, and other previously treated cases by sex and enter in respective columns of Block 1.
Add totals of columns 1-8/9 and enter in column 6.
Verify all patients registered during the quarter are accounted for in the report.
Similarly report smear-negative and extrapulmonary TB patients in Blocks 4 and 5.
Information for Block 6 is collected from TPT/IPT register; age groups below 15 years get 3HR, 15 years and above get 3HP; PLHIV get IPT.
Report presumptive TB cases among PLWHA in Blocks 8 and 8B.
Submit the report in triplicate: one copy to District Medical Officer, one to NTP HQ Dhaka, and one for records by 15th of next month.
fact_text: Quarterly TB case finding report (TB 10) requires counting and recording smear-positive, smear-negative, extrapulmonary, previously treated, and Xpert MTB/RIF positive cases by sex and age group, with specific blocks for each category and TPT data, submitted in triplicate by 15th of next month.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Reporting quarter for case finding, smear conversion and treatment result table
recommended_advice: Reports (case finding TB-10, smear conversion TB-12, treatment result TB-11) should be sent within two weeks after quarter end.
A year is divided into four quarters of three months each: 1st (Jan-Mar), 2nd (Apr-Jun), 3rd (Jul-Sep), 4th (Oct-Dec).
fact_text: Quarterly TB reports for case finding, smear conversion, and treatment results must be submitted within two weeks after quarter end, following the defined quarterly calendar.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Use Presumptive TB cases Referral Form (TB-14) for patients with cough ≥2 weeks, with or without other TB symptoms, for referral to nearest DOTS center.
Also use for household contacts, patients with unexplained cough, fever, weight loss, or night sweats for one week or more.
referral_criteria: Referral to nearest DOTS center for further examination.
fact_text: Patients with cough ≥2 weeks or unexplained cough, fever, weight loss, or night sweats for ≥1 week should be referred using TB-14 form to DOTS center for presumptive TB evaluation.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Quarterly Laboratory Performance Report (TB-13) replaces the previous TB-13 report and includes diagnostic and follow-up smear results, microscopy type, and Xpert MTB/RIF results.
This report is part of the smear rechecking system and included in the EQA SOP.
fact_text: Quarterly Laboratory Performance Report (TB-13) includes smear results, microscopy type, and Xpert MTB/RIF data as part of smear rechecking and EQA.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Quarterly report on sputum conversion at 2 or 3 months of treatment for smear-positive pulmonary TB patients should be prepared similarly to the case finding report.
followup_monitoring: Sputum smear results at end of 2 months (new bacteriologically confirmed TB) or 3 months (retreatment patients) are used to assess treatment response.
Unusually low conversion rates may indicate wrong categorization or poor treatment adherence.
Excessively high conversion rates may indicate poor quality microscopy (missing scanty or low grade positive smears).
fact_text: Quarterly sputum conversion reports at 2/3 months for smear-positive pulmonary TB patients help monitor treatment response and quality of microscopy.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Patient knowledge and satisfaction about TB disease, treatment duration, irregular treatment dangers, and availability of free treatment should be assessed.
fact_text: Assess patient knowledge on TB disease, treatment duration, irregular treatment risks, and free treatment availability.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Availability and completeness of treatment cards, laboratory registers, TB registers, and patient statistics (case registered, sputum conversion, treatment outcome) should be checked.
fact_text: Check completeness of treatment cards, lab registers, TB registers, and patient statistics for TB program monitoring.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Laboratory services should ensure microscope functioning, presence of fungus, preservation, sufficient stock of slides, containers, reagents, and quality assurance in smear examination.
fact_text: Ensure microscope functioning, sufficient slides, reagents, and quality assurance for sputum smear microscopy.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Case Notification Rate (CNR) is calculated as (Number of cases registered in last 4 quarters / Total population) x 100,000.
Case Detection Rate (CDR) is calculated as (Number of cases registered in last 4 quarters / Number of estimated cases in last 4 quarters) x 100.
Treatment Success Rate is calculated as (Number of new smear-positive cases declared cured or treatment completed / Total number of new smear-positive cases registered in the same period) x 100.
fact_text: CNR, CDR, and Treatment Success Rate are key TB program indicators calculated using quarterly case registration and population data.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: DOT provider and patient knowledge of TB disease and treatment should be assessed as satisfactory or not satisfactory.
ETB (Extra-pulmonary TB) manager activities should be documented as in place or not.
Childhood TB preventive therapy (IPT) eligibility and registration for under-5 children should be recorded quarterly.
fact_text: DOT provider and patient knowledge of TB disease and treatment, ETB manager activities, and childhood TB IPT registration for under-5 children should be documented regularly.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Supervisors should provide summary of major findings and recommendations/comments during supervision visits.
Supervisor names and signatures should be recorded.
fact_text: Supervision reports should include summary of major findings, recommendations, and supervisor signatures for accountability.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021

fact_text: This page is a TB patient treatment card template used for recording patient demographics, contact history, TB classification (pulmonary/extrapulmonary, bacteriological confirmation), treatment history, diagnostic test results (sputum microscopy, Xpert MTB/RIF), HIV test, and treatment adherence monitoring.
source_figure_or_table: Annex 3 TB-01 patient treatment card form

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Tuberculosis treatment card includes detailed daily drug intake recording, drug dosage, treatment outcome options (cured, treatment completed, failure, lost to follow-up, transferred out, not evaluated), and space for documenting drug reactions and medical officer signature.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: This page shows a TB patient registration form capturing patient demographics, TB registration number, treatment start date, patient category (New, Retreatment, Child), disease classification (Pulmonary, Pulmonary with sputum positive, Extra-pulmonary), and treatment outcome categories (New, Retreatment, Transfer in, Loss to Follow up, Others).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: TB register form includes patient identifiers, TB registration number, treatment unit, disease classification, treatment history codes (New, Treatment after loss to follow-up, Relapse, Treatment failure, Transfer in, Treatment unknown, Other), and remarks; treatment history codes must be entered appropriately for accurate recording and reporting.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Treatment history codes: N = New case; U = Treatment unknown; T = Transfer in; F = Treatment failure; R = Relapse; L = Treatment after loss to follow-up; O = Other (e.g., patient with unknown previous treatment history or DR TB patient transferred from another center).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
referral_criteria: Patient transferred out to another DOTS center must have the name of the reporting unit recorded
followup_monitoring: Follow-up sputum smear examinations at 2, 5, and 6 months
Record treatment outcome as cured, treatment completed, died, treatment failure, lost to follow-up, or transferred out
fact_text: TB treatment register includes fields for sputum smear results at 2, 5, and 6 months, treatment outcomes, HIV status, ART and CPT status, and remarks including transfer details.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Record Xpert MTB/RIF test results as follows: T = MTB detected, R = Rif resistant detected, RR = MTB detected, Rif resistant, T1 = MTB detected, Rif resistant indeterminate, N = MTB not detected, F = invalid or error
Record treatment outcome as cured, treatment completed, died, treatment failure, lost to follow-up, or transferred out
Treatment failure is defined as positive smear results on 2 or more consecutive occasions at 5 months and at the end of treatment or any cause of cure failure including drug resistance
Lost to follow-up is defined as a patient who interrupted treatment for 2 consecutive months or more
Patient transferred out must have the name of the reporting unit recorded
referral_criteria: Transfer out patients must have the name of the reporting unit recorded
fact_text: Definitions for treatment outcomes and Xpert MTB/RIF test result codes are provided for accurate recording and reporting in the TB register.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021

fact_text: The page contains a tuberculosis laboratory register form template for recording patient demographic details, specimen details, diagnostic test results (smear, Xpert MTB/RIF, culture), treatment/facility status, follow-up, and referral information to support TB case recording and reporting.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: AFB microscopy requested via form TB-05 for sputum specimens
Microscopy results to be recorded as Negative, Scanty (1-9 AFB), 1+, 2+, 3+
Microscopy methods include Ziehl-Neelsen (ZN) and LED fluorescence

fact_text: AFB microscopy for sputum is requested using form TB-05, with results recorded by microscopy method (ZN or LED) and graded as Negative, Scanty (1-9 AFB), 1+, 2+, or 3+.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: The form captures detailed patient identification, TB disease type (pulmonary or extrapulmonary), history of treatment failure, relapse, retreatment, and contact with DR-TB cases to classify drug-resistant TB cases.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Diagnosis and follow-up of DR-TB requires microscopy, Xpert MTB/RIF, culture, and Line Probe Assay tests as indicated.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Interpretation of DR-TB diagnostic tests includes MTB detection, rifampicin resistance status, culture positivity with colony counts, and drug susceptibility results for first- and second-line drugs.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Use the TB referral/transfer form to document patient details, bacteriological and clinical diagnosis, treatment type, treatment start date, and reasons for referral.
Send the form back to the referring unit as soon as treatment outcome is available.
Ensure the institution receiving the patient sends treatment outcome back to the referring center after treatment completion.
fact_text: A standardized TB referral/transfer form is used to document patient diagnosis, treatment, and referral details, and to ensure communication of treatment outcomes between referring and receiving units.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: Drug quantity for one quarter is calculated by multiplying the number of patients in each treatment category by the number of tablets needed per patient, with buffer stock included (100%). Specific formulas for each drug and category are provided in the table.
recommended_advice: Maintain minimum stock of one patient's medicine for each category at all times, even if no patients were registered in the previous quarter.
Avoid overstock by redistributing medicines to nearest low stock facilities before preparing next quarter's requisition.
fact_text: Drug requisition for first line TB drugs is calculated quarterly by multiplying registered patients in each treatment category by the required drug quantity per patient, including buffer stock; minimum stock must be maintained and overstock avoided by redistribution.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: This table (TB 10) is a standardized quarterly reporting form for all TB cases registered (excluding transfers) by age group, sex, and TB classification: pulmonary and extrapulmonary TB, bacteriologically confirmed and clinically diagnosed, new, relapse, treatment after loss to follow-up, treatment after failure, and others (unknown). It includes columns for treatment history and sex-disaggregated counts.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Table on TB patient data recording and reporting
fact_text: Page contains a detailed tabular format for recording and reporting TB-related data including patient referral source, sputum smear microscopy results, GeneXpert test results, X-ray activity, age groups of registered children, and TB/HIV activities, disaggregated by sex and other categories.
source_figure_or_table: Table on TB patient data recording and reporting

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Table TB 11: Quarterly Report on Treatment Outcome of TB Patients Registered 9-12 months earlier
fact_text: Quarterly reporting form for TB patients registered 9-12 months earlier includes detailed categories for treatment outcomes: successfully treated, died, failure, lost to follow-up, transferred out; disaggregated by type of TB (pulmonary bacteriologically confirmed, pulmonary clinically diagnosed, extrapulmonary) and age groups (0-14, 15+), with sex disaggregation and total counts.
source_figure_or_table: Table TB 11: Quarterly Report on Treatment Outcome of TB Patients Registered 9-12 months earlier

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: This table is a quarterly report form for sputum conversion at 2 months of pulmonary TB patients registered 3-6 months earlier, capturing bacteriological status (smear positive/negative), treatment history (new, relapse, treatment after failure, treatment after loss to follow-up, others previously treated), and clinical diagnosis status, disaggregated by sex and total.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Use the National Tuberculosis Control Program Laboratory Performance Report form to record and monitor sputum smear microscopy and Xpert MTB/RIF testing data quarterly.
Report total number of sputum smears examined, positive smears by grading, and smear-negative presumptive TB cases.
Record Xpert MTB/RIF results including MTB detected/not detected, rifampicin resistance detected/not detected, invalid/error, or no result.
Calculate and monitor positivity rates among presumptive TB cases and follow-up smear examinations to assess program performance.
Use this data for planning, supervision, and quality assurance of TB diagnostic services.
followup_monitoring: Quarterly update and review of laboratory performance data is required.
fact_text: Quarterly laboratory performance reporting includes sputum smear microscopy and Xpert MTB/RIF results with positivity rates to monitor and improve TB diagnostic services.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Contact history should be documented indicating contact with TB patient, DR TB patient, or no contact.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Previous TB treatment history should be recorded including diagnosis type (pulmonary or extrapulmonary), prior anti-TB treatment status, treatment source (private or government), treatment documentation availability, number of prior treatment occasions, treatment category (new, retreatment, DR TB, others), treatment completion status, and duration if treatment was not completed.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: The TPT Preventive Therapy Register records detailed demographic and treatment data for contacts eligible for TB preventive therapy, including age, sex, relation to source case, TPT regimen, start and completion dates, and outcomes.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: TPT eligibility criteria include: household contacts of pulmonary bacteriologically confirmed TB patients who have no active TB disease.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: TPT requires a full course of preventive treatment completed over 3 to 6 months.
fact_text: Preventive therapy for eligible contacts should be completed fully over 3 to 6 months to ensure effectiveness.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
followup_monitoring: Monitor for any adverse effects during the course of TPT.
fact_text: Patients on TPT should be monitored for adverse effects throughout the preventive therapy course.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Bacteriologically confirmed TB case is defined as a patient with a positive biological specimen by smear microscopy (LED or ZN) or culture (liquid or solid) or WHO recommended rapid diagnostic tests such as Xpert MTB/RIF, Xpert ULTRA, or TrueNat.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Clinically diagnosed TB case is defined as a patient who does not meet bacteriological confirmation criteria but is diagnosed with active TB by a registered physician based on strong clinical evidence including X-ray abnormalities or suggestive histology, and decision to treat is made.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Clinically diagnosed TB cases subsequently found to be bacteriologically confirmed (before or after treatment start) should be reclassified as bacteriologically confirmed cases.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Only bacteriologically confirmed or clinically diagnosed patients should be initiated on TB treatment; no patient should start trial TB treatment.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Presumptive TB is defined as a patient presenting with symptoms or signs suggestive of TB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: TB cases (bacteriologically confirmed or clinically diagnosed) are classified by anatomical site, history of previous treatment, drug resistance, and HIV status.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: All pulmonary TB cases must have sputum examined for TB by a National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) and WHO recommended diagnostic tool.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Extrapulmonary TB (EPTB) is any bacteriologically confirmed or clinically diagnosed TB involving organs other than lungs such as pleura, lymph nodes, larynx, meninges, abdomen, genitourinary tract, spine, bones, joints, skin.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Table: Classification based on drug resistance
fact_text: Mono-resistance: resistance to one first-line anti-TB drug only. Poly-resistance: resistance to more than one first-line drug except isoniazid and rifampicin together. MDR-TB: resistance to at least isoniazid and rifampicin. XDR-TB: MDR-TB plus resistance to moxifloxacin or levofloxacin and one other group A drug (BDQ, LZD). Rifampicin resistance (RR): resistance to rifampicin detected by phenotypic or genotypic methods.
source_figure_or_table: Table: Classification based on drug resistance

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Pulmonary TB (PTB) is any bacteriologically confirmed or clinically diagnosed TB involving lung parenchyma or tracheobronchial tree; miliary TB is classified as PTB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Table: Classification based on history of previous TB treatment
fact_text: Relapse: previously treated TB patients declared cured or treatment completed, now with recurrent TB episode (true relapse or reinfection). Treatment after failure: previously treated patients whose treatment failed most recent course. Treatment after loss to follow-up: previously treated patients declared lost to follow-up at end of most recent course. Other previously treated: previously treated patients with unknown or undocumented recent treatment outcome.
source_figure_or_table: Table: Classification based on history of previous TB treatment

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: HIV status unknown TB patient is any bacteriologically confirmed or clinically diagnosed TB case with no HIV test result and no documented HIV care enrolment; reclassify if HIV status later determined.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: HIV-negative TB patient is any bacteriologically confirmed or clinically diagnosed TB case with negative HIV test at TB diagnosis; if later found HIV-positive, reclassify accordingly.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: HIV-positive TB patient is any bacteriologically confirmed or clinically diagnosed TB case with positive HIV test at TB diagnosis or documented enrolment in HIV care.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Other category: patients not fitting transfer in/out, e.g., previously treated with erratic or unknown TB regimen or on trial ATT.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Transfer in: patient already registered for treatment in a DOTS centre and subsequently transferred to another DOTS centre.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Transfer out: patient transferred to another recording and reporting unit with unknown treatment outcome; occurs rarely.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Contacts of microbiologically confirmed TB patients, PLHIV, diabetics, malnourished, cancer patients, and immunosuppressed or steroid-treated patients should be regularly screened for TB signs and symptoms.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Additional pulmonary TB symptoms include respiratory: shortness of breath, chest pain, haemoptysis; and general: weight loss, loss of appetite, fever, night sweats.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Pulmonary TB should be presumed in persons with persistent cough for 2 weeks or more, with or without sputum production, despite broad-spectrum antibiotics without anti-TB effect.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: GeneXpert or sputum microscopy should always be requested for patients with cough lasting 2 weeks or longer, even if no other symptoms are present.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Children of all ages, especially under 5 years, and adolescents should be prioritized in all active case finding activities.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Elderly persons aged 65 and above should be prioritized in all active case finding activities.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Homeless or floating populations should be reached by outreach mobile vans or sputum smear centers in stations or terminals.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Household contacts of index TB cases should be traced and investigated as a priority group in active case finding.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: People living in congregate settings such as prisons, hostels, and orphanages should be screened and contact traced using outreach mobile vans.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: People with chronic diseases such as diabetes, COPD, and malnutrition should be prioritized during all active case finding activities.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Slum dwellers should be targeted for active case finding through household visits, outreach smear centers, or mobile vans at least once every quarter.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Three types of case finding under NTP: Passive Case Finding (patient reports symptoms), Intensified Case Finding (health staff search for TB symptoms among care seekers), Active Case Finding (community health workers seek TB symptoms among vulnerable populations).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Diagnosis of extrapulmonary TB should be made by a graduate physician or specialist and often requires special examinations such as GeneXpert MTB/RIF or ULTRA, X-ray, CT scan, MRI, biopsy, Fine Needle Aspiration Cytology (FNAC).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Common extrapulmonary TB presentations include: TB lymphadenitis (lymph node swelling), pleural effusion (fever, chest pain, shortness of breath), TB arthritis (joint pain and swelling), spinal TB (radiological findings with or without loss of function), and TB meningitis (headache, fever, neck stiffness, mental confusion).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Presumptive extrapulmonary TB is indicated by organ-specific symptoms such as lymph node swelling, joint pain and swelling, neck stiffness, disorientation, and constitutional symptoms like significant weight loss, persistent fever for 2 weeks or more, night sweats.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Presumptive pulmonary TB includes contacts of microbiologically confirmed TB patients with cough of any duration, presumptive or confirmed extrapulmonary TB with cough of any duration, and HIV positive patients with cough of any duration.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: All household contacts of smear-positive and drug-resistant TB patients should be examined for possible TB and actively approached for screening.
fact_text: All household contacts of smear-positive and DR-TB patients must be actively screened for TB by health workers or community volunteers.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Health workers and community volunteers should identify and refer presumptive TB patients for sputum examination and other investigations for early diagnosis and treatment.
fact_text: Health workers and community volunteers must identify and refer presumptive TB patients for sputum examination and further investigations.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Non-medical community members including Shasthya Shebikas, village doctors, cured TB patients, and community leaders should motivate presumptive TB cases to visit health facilities for diagnosis and management.
fact_text: Non-medical community members should encourage presumptive TB patients to seek sputum examination and appropriate management at health facilities.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Medical doctors at government and NGO health facilities are responsible for identifying presumptive TB cases and arranging appropriate investigations including CXR, sputum microscopy, Xpert MTB/RIF, and TrueNat.
referral_criteria: Extra-pulmonary presumptive TB cases should be referred to appropriate specialists/facilities.
fact_text: Medical doctors must identify presumptive TB cases and arrange investigations like CXR, sputum microscopy, Xpert MTB/RIF, and TrueNat; extra-pulmonary presumptive TB should be referred to specialists.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021

fact_text: TB diagnosis laboratory network pyramid: National TB Reference Laboratory (NTRL) at top (1), Regional TB Reference Laboratories (RTRL) and CDC/District Level labs (5+44), Peripheral labs including UHC/GeneXpert/Microscopy Centers (1170).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: NTP staff proficiency ensured by technical training and periodic supervision of regional labs
Quality assurance implemented for regional and tertiary labs including chest disease clinics and hospitals
Guidance and strategic oversight provided to strengthen TB laboratory network and ensure quality and efficient use of services
fact_text: NTP ensures quality and proficiency of TB diagnostic labs through training, supervision, quality assurance, and strategic oversight.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: National TB Reference Laboratory acts as supervising reference lab for regional labs and performs culture, DST (1st & 2nd line), molecular tests, microscopy, and sequencing in special situations.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: WHO recommended alternative diagnostic tools including TrueNat, Line Probe Assay (LPA), and Xpert MTB	extbackslash XDR will be scaled up in a phased manner across the country.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: WHO recommends testing all presumptive TB patients by rapid molecular diagnostic tests like Xpert MTB/RIF (GeneXpert) where available.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Chest X-ray is a very sensitive screening tool for TB; abnormal findings require further microbiological confirmation, but X-ray can support diagnosis of clinically diagnosed TB and extrapulmonary TB such as pleural effusion, pericardial effusion, mediastinal adenopathy, and miliary TB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Culture of TB bacilli is the gold standard for diagnosis, detecting a higher proportion of patients among presumptive TB cases and able to detect low numbers of bacilli.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: NTRL and RTRL perform liquid culture (MGIT) and Line Probe Assay (LPA) of second-line drugs for confirmed rifampicin-resistant TB cases to ensure early diagnosis of PreXDR and XDR TB; bacteriological examinations including smear microscopy, culture-DST, GeneXpert, and LPA are provided free of cost.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Sputum smear microscopy is simple, inexpensive, requires minimum training, has high specificity and reliability, and is feasible at peripheral health institutions; it is used for diagnosis and monitoring progress in pulmonary TB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Tuberculin skin test (Mantoux) at standard dose is used to diagnose latent TB infection (LTBI) and to support TB diagnosis in children; it does not confirm active TB disease and may yield false positives or negatives in certain conditions such as prior NTM exposure or immunocompromised states.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
referral_criteria: specialist centers at district level equipped with FNAC, histopathology, GeneXpert for EPTB diagnosis
fact_text: FNAC, biopsy, histopathology, and GeneXpert are special tests for confirmation of extrapulmonary TB; at least one district-level center will be equipped for these tests.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: Liquid culture system (MGIT) detects mycobacterial growth faster (within 14 days) and DST results are available 14-26 days after culture positivity; requires specialized containment lab.
contraindications_or_cautions: liquid culture requires TB Containment Lab, operationally challenging
fact_text: Liquid culture system (MGIT) detects mycobacterial growth faster (within 14 days) and DST results are available 14-26 days after culture positivity; requires specialized containment lab.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Culture is highly sensitive and specific for TB diagnosis but requires 2-8 weeks for results; used mainly for follow-up in drug-resistant TB to detect early recurrence.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
contraindications_or_cautions: requires uninterrupted power supply, temperature control, well-trained staff
fact_text: GeneXpert MTB/RIF (CB-NAAT) detects Mycobacterium tuberculosis DNA and rifampicin resistance from sputum in 105 minutes; suitable for deployment at all health facility levels with operational requirements.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
contraindications_or_cautions: requires moderate risk level TB lab with at least 3 clean rooms, operationally difficult to create and maintain
fact_text: Line Probe Assay (LPA) detects resistance genes for rifampicin, isoniazid, fluoroquinolones, and second line injectables; requires smear positive samples and inoculation on culture if smear negative.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: phenotypic DST using solid and liquid media (MGIT)
fact_text: Phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (DST) using solid and liquid media (MGIT) is used for first and second line drugs after standardization.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Patients should be instructed clearly on sputum collection technique: collect sputum in open air away from others, avoid saliva, collect 2-5 ml of mucoid or mucopurulent sputum in a sterile container rinsed with clean water.
fact_text: Clear patient instructions are essential for quality sputum collection: collect 2-5 ml mucoid/mucopurulent sputum in sterile container after rinsing mouth, in open air away from others.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Outreach sputum collection camps organized by NGOs and government field staff provide sputum containers and counseling; patients bring early morning sputum and spot specimen is collected at camp using a second pot.
fact_text: Outreach sputum collection camps provide containers and counseling; patients bring early morning sputum and spot specimen is collected at camp using a second container.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Sputum collected at referring health facilities must be transported to nearest microscopy or GeneXpert site within 2 days; containers and samples must be disinfected with 5% phenol solution and disposed as per guidelines after smear results are recorded.
fact_text: Sputum samples from referring facilities must reach microscopy or GeneXpert sites within 2 days; containers must be disinfected with 5% phenol and disposed according to guidelines after smear results are recorded.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: If microscopy or Xpert MTB/RIF facilities are available, patients should bring sputum specimens to the responsible staff or laboratory promptly; if delay occurs, specimens should be refrigerated up to one week.
fact_text: Sputum specimens should be transported promptly to microscopy or Xpert MTB/RIF facilities; if delay is unavoidable, refrigerate specimens up to one week to inhibit microbial growth.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Early morning sputum is preferable for Xpert MTB/RIF testing, but spot specimen collection is acceptable depending on patient convenience.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Two sputum specimens are recommended for microscopy: an 'on-the-spot' specimen collected when the patient is identified as presumptive pulmonary TB, and an early morning specimen collected at home the next day.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Radiological, cytological, pathological, biochemical, immunological investigations
fact_text: Extra-pulmonary TB (EPTB) includes TB of pleura, lymph nodes, intestine, genito-urinary tract, joints, bones, meninges; presents with constitutional symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss) and local site features; positive contact history supports suspicion; diagnosis supported by CB-NAAT, liquid culture, and special investigations (radiological, cytological, pathological, biochemical, immunological).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_medicines: First line drugs (FLD) for MTB detected without RR
Second line drugs (FLD) for MTB detected with RR
fact_text: Presumptive TB cases at microscopy sites undergo sputum smear; if positive, test by GeneXpert if available or start treatment; if negative, further clinical evaluation including CXR and GeneXpert if suggestive; GeneXpert sites test directly with GeneXpert; MTB detected without rifampicin resistance treated with first line drugs; MTB with rifampicin resistance treated with second line drugs; repeat GeneXpert if invalid or indeterminate rifampicin resistance.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Tuberculous lymphadenopathy diagnosis relies on FNAC (AFB smear, Xpert MTB/RIF, ULTRA) or biopsy histopathology; lymph nodes involved are mainly cervical and others; disease course includes firm nodes progressing to abscess and sinus formation.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Biochemical tests such as exudate analysis
Cytological examination of effusions, ascites, CSF fluid
fact_text: Biochemical tests (exudate) and cytological examination of effusions, ascites, and CSF fluid are supportive investigations for EPTB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Culture for AFB from pleural, pericardial, ascitic, cerebrospinal fluids, urine, aspirate (FNAC) from solid organs like lymph node, spine, epididymis
fact_text: Culture for AFB is recommended on bodily fluids (pleural, pericardial, ascitic, cerebrospinal, urine) and aspirates from solid organs (lymph node, spine, epididymis) for EPTB diagnosis.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Histopathological or cytopathological examination of biopsy material from lymph node, peritoneum, synovium, spine, bone, liver, spleen, genital tract
fact_text: Histopathological or cytopathological examination detecting caseating granulomas on biopsy from lymph node, peritoneum, synovium, spine, bone, liver, spleen, genital tract is strongly suggestive of tuberculosis.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Imaging studies (X-rays, CT scan, ultrasound) of involved region such as lung/chest, spine, bone, joint, adrenal gland
fact_text: Imaging (X-rays, CT scan, ultrasound) of involved regions (lung, chest, spine, bone, joint, adrenal gland) supports EPTB diagnosis.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Molecular tests (Xpert MTB/RIF or ULTRA) on pleural, pericardial, ascitic, cerebrospinal, synovial fluids, FNAC, tissue, lymph node aspirate, lymph node biopsy, pus
fact_text: Molecular tests (Xpert MTB/RIF or ULTRA) are recommended for EPTB diagnosis on pleural, pericardial, ascitic, cerebrospinal, synovial fluids, FNAC, tissue, lymph node aspirate, biopsy, and pus samples.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Tuberculin skin test (Mantoux) and Interferon Gamma Release Assays (IGRA) are supportive tests for EPTB diagnosis.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Bacteriological confirmation of miliary TB is sometimes possible from sputum, cerebrospinal fluid, bone marrow, liver or blood; granulomas may be evident in liver or bone marrow biopsy specimens.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Testing of bronchoalveolar lavage is more likely to lead to bacteriological confirmation in miliary TB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Ascites in TB results from peritoneal TB; routes of spread include tuberculous mesenteric lymph nodes, intestinal TB with ulcers/fistulae from swallowed infected sputum, and blood-borne spread.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Closed pleural biopsy using Abrams needle is useful for histological diagnosis of pleural TB with about 75% diagnostic yield; multiple biopsies or small open biopsy increase yield further.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Tuberculous serous effusions usually present with constitutional and local features; microscopy/Xpert MTB/RIF of aspirate rarely shows AFB due to inflammatory reaction.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Interpret protein concentration cautiously in aspirated fluid from tuberculous serous effusions; protein >30 g/l suggests exudate but delay in lab analysis may lower protein result.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Miliary TB diagnosis is based on chest X-ray showing diffuse, uniformly distributed small milary shadows resembling 'like small millet seeds'.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Diagnosis of tuberculous pericardial effusion relies on constitutional and cardiovascular features plus ECG, chest X-ray and echocardiography findings.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Pleural effusion diagnosis is clinical and by chest X-ray; ultrasound confirms fluid presence; fluid is usually straw-colored with high lymphocytes; pus indicates empyema.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Abdominal TB diagnosis relies on ascitic fluid analysis, ultrasound, and peritoneal biopsy, with laparoscopy preferred for biopsy due to higher yield and lower complication rate.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Gastrointestinal TB commonly presents with abdominal pain, chronic diarrhoea, obstruction, haematochezia, right iliac fossa mass, fever, weight loss, night sweats, and doughy abdomen.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Genitourinary TB presents with urinary frequency, dysuria, haematuria, loin pain, or may be asymptomatic; urine pyuria and haematuria are common, and sterile pyuria suggests renal TB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Joint TB presents with pain, swelling, and limping, often with prior trauma history; diagnosis requires synovial biopsy and shows bone erosions and joint space narrowing on imaging.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Aspiration or bone biopsy for histopathology and culture
fact_text: Spinal TB diagnosis involves imaging (X-ray, CT, MRI) showing vertebral erosion and disc narrowing, with aspiration or biopsy confirming TB histopathology and culture.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: CNS tuberculosis is mainly a childhood TB manifestation but may also affect adults.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_tests: Biopsy and culture from genital specimens
fact_text: Genital TB diagnosis requires biopsy/culture from genital specimens; urine AFB/Xpert and culture of 3 morning urine samples aid urinary TB diagnosis.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Hepatic and splenic TB diagnosis relies on imaging (ultrasound/CT) and guided FNAC to identify abscesses or lesions.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Rare EPTB forms include ocular TB, nasopharyngeal TB mimicking Wegener's, various cutaneous TB lesions, and adrenal TB causing adrenal insufficiency.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Patients who fail to respond to first-line anti-TB drugs should be tested with GeneXpert and both 1st and 2nd line DST (LPA, liquid culture & DST) and managed as per drug-resistant TB guidelines.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Basic principles of TB treatment include prescribing an appropriate combination of drugs, administering drugs for the required duration (several months), and ensuring correct dosage to achieve optimum therapeutic effect.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Short Course Chemotherapy (SCC) is the recommended treatment for tuberculosis, aiming to render the patient non-infectious, cure TB, prevent death and relapse, and prevent acquired drug resistance.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: 2 months intensive phase, 4 months continuation phase
fact_text: Previously treated TB patients with DST showing susceptibility to rifampicin and isoniazid should receive Category 1 regimen: 2 months HRZE + 4 months HR; treatment extension for certain EPTB forms is based on clinical decision.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
referral_criteria: Patients bacteriologically positive but not yet registered or started on treatment should be traced within two weeks after lab result and started on appropriate treatment.
followup_monitoring: Medical officer or TB manager should conduct weekly review and cross-check TB register with laboratory register to ensure all diagnosed patients are registered and enrolled for treatment.
fact_text: Patients bacteriologically positive but not yet registered or started on treatment should be traced within two weeks and started on treatment; weekly review of TB and lab registers is recommended to ensure all diagnosed patients are registered and treated.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_medicines: HRZE (isoniazid, rifampicin, pyrazinamide, ethambutol) for 2 months intensive phase
HR (isoniazid, rifampicin) for 4 months continuation phase
dose_or_duration: 2 months intensive phase, 4 months continuation phase
fact_text: New drug-sensitive TB patients receive standard regimen of 4 drugs (HRZE) for 2 months intensive phase and 2 drugs (HR) for 4 months continuation phase.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
trigger_evidence: certain forms of extrapulmonary TB (CNS TB, skeletal TB, disseminated TB)
dose_or_duration: treatment duration may be extended based on clinical decision
fact_text: Treatment duration may be extended for certain extrapulmonary TB forms (CNS TB, skeletal TB, disseminated TB) based on clinical decision of treating physician on a case-by-case basis.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Table: Standardized treatment regimen for each diagnostic category (adults)
fact_text: Complicated extrapulmonary TB cases (TB meningitis, neurological TB, bone TB, non-resolving lymph node) receive 12 months of HRZE-Lfx regimen.
source_figure_or_table: Table: Standardized treatment regimen for each diagnostic category (adults)

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: If rifampicin resistance is detected, an MDR-TB regimen should be prescribed per recent drug-resistant TB treatment guidelines.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: All clinically diagnosed pulmonary TB cases with previous treatment history receive 6 months of 4-drug regimen (6HRZE).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Table: Standardized treatment regimen for each diagnostic category (adults)
fact_text: New cases including bacteriologically positive/negative PTB, extrapulmonary TB, and TB/HIV co-infected receive 2 months intensive phase (2 HRZE) and 4 months continuation phase (4 HR).
source_figure_or_table: Table: Standardized treatment regimen for each diagnostic category (adults)

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Patients with rifampicin-susceptible but isoniazid-resistant TB or unknown INH resistance receive a 5-drug regimen for 6 months (6 H/REZ-Lfx).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Table: Standardized treatment regimen for each diagnostic category (adults)
fact_text: Previously treated TB cases without resistance to TB drugs receive 6 months of HRZE regimen; clinically diagnosed PTB cases receive 6 months HRZE.
source_figure_or_table: Table: Standardized treatment regimen for each diagnostic category (adults)

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Treatment of drug-susceptible TB includes two phases: intensive phase (IP) daily for 2 months with 4 drugs (4FDC) and continuation phase (CP) daily for 4 months with 2 drugs (2FDC).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: Continuation phase is daily for 4 months (120 doses) and should be stopped after 120 doses; extension allowed only for certain severe forms of extrapulmonary TB.
fact_text: Continuation phase is daily for 4 months (120 doses) and should be stopped after 120 doses; extension allowed only for certain severe forms of extrapulmonary TB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: Drugs should be given daily; intensive phase is 2 months (60 doses) and should not be extended beyond 60 doses for any reason.
fact_text: Drugs should be given daily; intensive phase is 2 months (60 doses) and should not be extended beyond 60 doses for any reason.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: Treatment dosages are based on weight bands and should be modified if patient weight changes during treatment.
fact_text: Treatment dosages are based on weight bands and should be modified if patient weight changes during treatment.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: FDC tablets composition: 4 FDC contains isoniazid 75 mg + rifampicin 150 mg + pyrazinamide 400 mg + ethambutol 275 mg; 2 FDC contains isoniazid 75 mg + rifampicin 150 mg.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Fixed-dose combination (FDC) tablets are recommended over separate drug formulations for treatment of patients with drug-susceptible TB.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
recommended_advice: Monitor sputum smear microscopy at end of 2nd month (end of intensive phase), 5th month, and 6th month (end of treatment) for pulmonary TB patients.
For smear-negative patients at start, sputum should be examined at end of 2nd month.
If extrapulmonary TB patient develops chest symptoms, sputum should be collected and examined by smear microscopy and GeneXpert.
If sputum smear positive during follow-up, collect additional samples for Xpert MTB/RIF testing.
Patients smear positive at end of intensive phase but Xpert MTB/RIF sensitive for rifampicin should continue continuation phase treatment.
Clinical monitoring includes periodic assessment of symptoms and weight gain, especially for extrapulmonary and clinically diagnosed pulmonary TB.
Patient weight should be monitored monthly and drug doses adjusted if weight band changes.
Adherence should be monitored by reviewing treatment cards for drug intake and collection during intensive and continuation phases, including patient interviews.
followup_monitoring: Sputum smear microscopy at 2nd, 5th, and 6th months
GeneXpert testing if smear positive during follow-up
Monthly weight monitoring and dose adjustment
Clinical symptom and weight gain monitoring
Adherence monitoring via treatment card review and patient interview
fact_text: Pulmonary TB patients require sputum smear monitoring at 2nd, 5th, and 6th months; smear-positive follow-up samples need Xpert MTB/RIF testing; clinical and weight monitoring monthly; adherence monitored by treatment card review and patient interview.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Table: Weight band dosing for TB treatment phases
dose_or_duration: Drug-susceptible TB treatment dosing by weight band: Intensive phase (first 2 months) 4FDC daily tablets and continuation phase (next 4 months) 2FDC daily tablets; INH resistant regimen 4FDC for 6 months plus Levofloxacin 250 mg for 6 months with tablet numbers adjusted by weight bands: 30-37 kg: 2 tablets; 38-54 kg: 3 tablets; 55-70 kg: 4 tablets; >70 kg: 5 tablets.
fact_text: Drug-susceptible TB treatment dosing by weight band for intensive phase (4FDC daily, 2 months) and continuation phase (2FDC daily, 4 months) and INH resistant regimen (4FDC + Levofloxacin 250 mg daily for 6 months) with tablet numbers adjusted by weight bands.
source_figure_or_table: Table: Weight band dosing for TB treatment phases

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: For new pulmonary TB patients treated with a Rifampicin-containing regimen, extension of the intensive phase is not needed.
fact_text: Extension of intensive phase is not needed for new pulmonary TB patients treated with Rifampicin-containing regimens.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
referral_criteria: If a patient is found to harbor a drug-resistant strain of TB at any time during therapy, treatment is declared failed and the patient should be referred for DR-TB management.
fact_text: Any patient found to have drug-resistant TB during therapy should be declared treatment failure and referred for DR-TB management.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
source_section: Schedule for follow-up sputum examination in pulmonary bacteriologically confirmed TB patients
fact_text: For pulmonary bacteriologically confirmed TB patients, sputum smear examination is scheduled at end of month 2 (intensive phase), and at end of months 5 and 6 (continuation phase). If smear negative at month 2, start continuation phase treatment. If smear positive at month 2, test with Xpert MTB/RIF; if rifampicin sensitive, start continuation phase; if rifampicin resistant, declare treatment failure and start drug-resistant TB management. At months 5 and 6, if smear positive, declare treatment failure and evaluate/manage for drug resistance.
source_figure_or_table: Schedule for follow-up sputum examination in pulmonary bacteriologically confirmed TB patients

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: All extrapulmonary TB patients receive the same treatment regimen as pulmonary TB: 2 months intensive phase (2HRZE) followed by 4 months continuation phase (4HR).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: For TB lymphadenitis, if no improvement after 6 months treatment, continuation phase may be extended up to 10 months and patient should be investigated for drug-resistant TB at 6 months.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: For complicated/severe extrapulmonary TB, total treatment may be extended to 12 months: 2 months intensive phase (HRZE) plus up to 10 months continuation phase (HR), decided at end of 6 months treatment.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Treatment of osteoarticular and spinal TB (Pott's disease) is 12 months: 2 months intensive phase (HRZE) plus 10 months continuation phase (HR).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: Dexamethasone dosing for CNS TB: 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/day for 2-4 weeks, then tapered weekly by 0.1 mg/kg/week until 0.1 mg/kg/day, then tapered over 1 week; total duration usually 12 weeks.
fact_text: Dexamethasone dosing for CNS TB: 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/day for 2-4 weeks, then tapered weekly by 0.1 mg/kg/week until 0.1 mg/kg/day, then tapered over 1 week; total duration usually 12 weeks.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
dose_or_duration: Prednisolone dose for TB meningitis is 0.5–1 mg/kg daily, increased to 2 mg/kg daily in severe patients for 4 weeks, then tapered gradually over 4 to 8 weeks (total 1-2 months).
fact_text: Prednisolone dose for TB meningitis is 0.5–1 mg/kg daily, increased to 2 mg/kg daily in severe patients for 4 weeks, then tapered gradually over 4 to 8 weeks (total 1-2 months).

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Adjunct corticosteroid therapy (dexamethasone or prednisolone) is recommended for TB meningitis and TB pericarditis, tapered over 6-8 weeks.

source_title: National Guideline and Operational Manual for Tuberculosis 2021
fact_text: Treatment duration for TB meningitis is 12 months due to uncertain blood-brain barrier penetration of anti-TB drugs.
